weeks.title: Accounting concepts and the accounting equation
weeks.summary: Is week aap samjhoge ki accounting business ki language kyun hai, kaunse basic concepts (entity, going concern, accrual, consistency, conservatism) har record ke peeche chalte hain, aur accounting equation Assets = Liabilities + Equity har transaction ke baad bhi balance kyun rehti hai.
concepts: **Accounting** business ke transactions ko record, classify aur summarise karke unke users tak pahunchane ka system hai. Users: investors (kya profit ho raha hai?), lenders aur bank (loan wapas milega?), government (tax), aur managers (decisions). **Financial accounting** bahar ke users ke liye fixed format me statements banata hai; management accounting andar ke decisions ke liye. Is course me hum Ind AS / IFRS wale terms use karenge: revenue, statement of profit and loss, balance sheet.

**Business entity concept**: business aur uska owner do alag entities hain. Agar Ananya apni bakery 'Kaveri Bakes' ke cash se ghar ka ration khareedti hai to wo business ka expense nahi, **drawings** hai (owner ki equity kam hoti hai). Company ke case me ye aur clear hai — company legally bhi shareholders se alag hai.

**Money measurement aur historical cost**: sirf wahi cheezein record hoti hain jinhe paise me measure kar sakein (team ki motivation record nahi hoti). Assets generally us cost par record hote hain jo unhe khareedte waqt di gayi thi, aaj ki market value par nahi (kuch exceptions Ind AS me hain, par basic rule cost hai).

**Going concern**: maana jaata hai ki business aage bhi chalta rahega, band hone wala nahi hai. Isi wajah se machine ko 'cost minus depreciation' par dikhate hain, scrap ya distress-sale value par nahi. Agar business sach me band hone wala ho to ye assumption tootta hai aur basis badal jaata hai.

**Accrual concept**: revenue tab record hota hai jab earn hua (goods deliver ya service di), aur expense tab jab incur hua — cash kab aaya ya gaya, isse fark nahi padta. Isi ke saath **matching**: jis period ka revenue hai, usi period me uska related expense dikhao, taaki profit sahi aaye.

**Consistency**: ek baar method chuna (jaise inventory ke liye FIFO, ya depreciation ke liye straight line) to har saal wahi use karo, taaki saalon ke numbers compare ho sakein. Change sirf valid reason par, aur notes me disclose karke.

**Conservatism (prudence)**: uncertainty me savdhaan raho — expected losses ko jaldi pehchano, par gains tab tak record mat karo jab tak pakke na hon. Example: inventory 'lower of cost and net realisable value (NRV)' par, aam taur par item-by-item. Ind AS framework me prudence ka matlab caution hai, jaan-bujh kar numbers chhote dikhana nahi.

**Accounting equation**: Assets = Liabilities + Equity. Assets = business ke resources; liabilities = bahar walon ka claim; equity = owner ka claim (capital + profits − drawings). Har transaction kam se kam do jagah asar daalta hai (dual aspect), isliye equation hamesha balance rehti hai.

example.problem: Ananya ne fictional bakery 'Kaveri Bakes' shuru ki. Transactions: (1) ₹2,00,000 cash capital laayi, (2) bank se ₹50,000 loan liya, (3) ₹80,000 cash me oven khareeda, (4) ₹20,000 ka flour credit par khareeda (abhi use nahi hua), (5) cakes bech kar ₹30,000 cash kamaya, (6) ₹8,000 salary cash me di. Last me accounting equation banao.
steps: (2) Cash +50,000 aur Liabilities (loan) +50,000. (3) Cash −80,000, Oven +80,000 — sirf assets ki shakal badli, total same.
(5) Cash +30,000 aur Equity +30,000 (revenue profit badhata hai). (6) Cash −8,000 aur Equity −8,000 (expense profit ghatata hai).
Answer: **Assets ₹2,92,000 = Liabilities ₹70,000 + Equity ₹2,22,000** — equation balance hai.

mistakes: Owner ke personal kharch ko business expense likh dena. Entity concept ke hisaab se wo drawings hai — equity kam hogi, profit nahi.
Cash aane ko hi revenue samajhna. Advance mila par kaam abhi baaki hai to wo revenue nahi, liability hai; aur kaam ho gaya par paisa baad me aayega to bhi revenue isi period ka hai.
Conservatism ko 'sab kuch kam dikhao' samajh lena. Rule hai: loss ka andaza ho to record karo, gain ka sirf pakka hone par — numbers ko jaan-bujh kar ghatana nahi.
revision: Assets = Liabilities + Equity, har transaction ke baad.
Entity: owner ka personal kharch = drawings, expense nahi.
Going concern ⇒ assets cost minus depreciation par, liquidation value par nahi.
Accrual: earn/incur hone par record, cash ke time par nahi.
Inventory = lower of cost and NRV (item-by-item).

questions.question: Ravi apni cycle repair shop ke cash box se ₹5,000 nikaal kar ghar ka ration khareedta hai. Kaunsa concept kehta hai ki ise business expense nahi, drawings record karo?
questions.explanation: Business entity concept business aur owner ko alag maanta hai, isliye owner ka personal kharch drawings hai (equity ghatti hai), expense nahi. Accrual sirf timing batata hai — kab record karna hai — kis ka kharch hai ye nahi.

questions.question: Ek business ke total assets ₹8,00,000 aur total liabilities ₹3,50,000 hain. Owner ki equity kitni hai?
questions.explanation: Equity = Assets − Liabilities = 8,00,000 − 3,50,000 = ₹4,50,000. ₹11,50,000 tab aata hai jab liabilities ko assets me jod dete ho — liabilities bahar walon ka claim hai, unhe ghatana hota hai.

questions.question: Ek consulting firm ka financial year 31 March ko khatam hota hai. March me usne ₹60,000 ki service deliver ki jiska payment April me aayega. March me hi use ₹10,000 advance mila April me hone wale kaam ke liye. Accrual concept se is saal (March tak) ka revenue kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Revenue tab record hota hai jab earn ho: March me di gayi service ka ₹60,000 is saal ka revenue hai, cash baad me aaye to bhi. ₹10,000 advance ka kaam abhi hua nahi, isliye wo liability hai. ₹70,000 tab aata hai jab advance ko bhi revenue maan lete ho.

questions.question: Year-end par ek shop ke paas do items hain. Item X: cost ₹1,20,000, NRV ₹1,05,000. Item Y: cost ₹50,000, NRV ₹70,000. Lower of cost and NRV rule item-by-item lagao. Balance sheet me inventory kitni dikhegi?
questions.explanation: Har item ka lower value lo: X = min(1,20,000, 1,05,000) = 1,05,000; Y = min(50,000, 70,000) = 50,000. Total = ₹1,55,000. ₹1,70,000 tab aata hai jab dono ka total cost (1,70,000) aur total NRV (1,75,000) compare karte ho — usse X ka ₹15,000 loss Y ke gain ke peeche chhup jaata hai.

questions.question: Ek factory ki machine aaj scrap me sirf ₹40,000 me bikegi, par balance sheet me wo ₹3,00,000 (cost minus depreciation) par dikhayi gayi hai. Ye kis assumption ki wajah se sahi hai?
questions.explanation: Going concern maanta hai ki business chalta rahega aur machine se aage bhi kaam lega, isliye usse cost minus depreciation par dikhate hain, scrap value par nahi. Conservatism ka trap lagta hai, par wo uncertain losses ke liye hai — chalti hui machine ko scrap value par girana uska kaam nahi.

questions.question: Ek business ki shuruaat me Assets ₹5,00,000 aur Liabilities ₹2,00,000 hain. Phir: (i) creditors ko ₹40,000 cash diye, (ii) ₹70,000 ki service credit par di, (iii) ₹15,000 rent cash me diya, (iv) owner ne ₹10,000 personal use ke liye nikaale. End me equity kitni hai?
questions.explanation: Opening equity = 5,00,000 − 2,00,000 = 3,00,000. Revenue +70,000, rent −15,000, drawings −10,000 ⇒ ₹3,45,000. Creditor payment se cash aur liability dono 40,000 ghatte hain, equity par asar nahi. ₹3,05,000 usi 40,000 ko equity se ghatane ka trap hai; ₹3,55,000 drawings bhoolne se aata hai. Check: assets 5,05,000 = liabilities 1,60,000 + equity 3,45,000.

questions.question: Ek company pichhle 5 saal se machines par straight line method se depreciation lagati thi. Is saal bina kisi valid reason ke usne WDV method apna liya, sirf taaki profit alag dikhe. Kaunsa concept toota?
questions.explanation: Consistency kehta hai ki ek baar chuna method har saal chalao, taaki saalon ke numbers compare ho sakein; change sirf valid reason par aur notes me disclose karke. Going concern ka trap lagta hai kyunki depreciation se juda hai, par wo sirf ye maanta hai ki business chalta rahega — method badalne ka sawaal nahi.

questions.question: 'Kaveri Bakes' ne 2018 me ek dukaan ki zameen ₹12,00,000 me khareedi thi. Aaj uski market value ₹30,00,000 hai. Basic historical cost rule ke hisaab se balance sheet me zameen kitne par dikhegi?
questions.explanation: Historical cost concept: asset us cost par record hota hai jo khareedte waqt diya, aaj ki market value par nahi (land par depreciation bhi nahi lagta). ₹30,00,000 market value hai, ₹18,00,000 sirf value ka badhna hai, aur ₹42,00,000 dono ko jodne ka galat tareeka hai.

questions.question: Ek company ko lagta hai ki wo ek court case jeet jaayegi aur agle saal use ₹3,00,000 milenge, par faisla abhi aaya nahi hai. Conservatism (prudence) ke hisaab se is saal kya karna chahiye?
options: Aadha, yaani ₹1,50,000 income abhi record karo
Abhi ₹3,00,000 asset aur utni hi liability record karo
Abhi koi income record nahi; pakka hone par karenge
questions.explanation: Prudence: expected losses jaldi pehchano, par gains tab tak record mat karo jab tak pakke na hon. Case abhi jeeta nahi gaya, isliye koi income nahi. 'Aadha record karo' ek compromise jaisa lagta hai, par uncertain gain ka koi bhi hissa abhi income nahi banta.

questions.question: Ek business ne ₹60,000 ki machine khareedi: ₹20,000 cash diye aur baaki supplier ko baad me dene hain. Accounting equation par kya asar hoga?
options: Assets +₹60,000, Liabilities +₹60,000, Equity par asar nahi
Assets +₹40,000, Equity +₹40,000, Liabilities par asar nahi
Assets +₹40,000, Liabilities +₹40,000, Equity par asar nahi
questions.explanation: Machine +60,000 aur cash −20,000, to net assets +40,000. Supplier ka baaki 40,000 liability hai. Koi income ya expense nahi, isliye equity same. 'Assets +₹60,000' cash ka ghatna bhool jaata hai, aur equity badhana galat hai kyunki machine khareedna profit nahi hai.

questions.question: Ek trader ne March me ₹1,00,000 cost ka maal ₹1,50,000 me credit par becha; customer April me payment karega. Is sale par salesman ko 5% commission (sale value par) April me milega. Financial year 31 March ko khatam hota hai. Accrual aur matching se is sale ka March tak ka profit kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Revenue March me earn hua: 1,50,000. Matching se usi sale ke expenses bhi March me: cost 1,00,000 + commission 1,50,000 × 5% = 7,500. Profit = ₹42,500. ₹50,000 commission ko April ka maan leta hai (cash timing), ₹0 cash basis ki soch hai, aur ₹45,000 commission ko cost par lagane se aata hai.

questions.question: Ek business ki shuruaat me Assets ₹3,00,000 = Liabilities ₹1,00,000 + Equity ₹2,00,000 hai. Phir: (i) owner ne ₹50,000 extra capital cash me daala, (ii) ₹30,000 ka maal credit par khareeda, (iii) ₹20,000 cost ka maal ₹28,000 me credit par becha, (iv) bank loan ka ₹12,000 principal chukaya, (v) ₹5,000 interest cash me diya. End me total assets aur equity kitne hain?

Ek proprietor ke business ka saal ka data: cash sales ₹4,00,000; saal ke end par credit sales ke ₹50,000 abhi customers par baaki; cash me diye gaye kharch ₹2,20,000, jisme ₹30,000 owner ke ghar ka bijli bill hai; saal ka ₹15,000 rent abhi dena baaki hai. Accrual aur business entity concept se business ka profit kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Revenue = 4,00,000 + 50,000 = 4,50,000 (credit sales bhi earn ho chuki). Expenses = 2,20,000 − 30,000 (ghar ka bill drawings hai) + 15,000 (outstanding rent) = 2,05,000. Profit = ₹2,45,000. ₹1,80,000 seedha cash basis hai; ₹2,15,000 owner ke bill ko business expense maan leta hai; ₹2,60,000 baaki rent bhool jaata hai.

questions.question: Year-end par ek shop ke paas teen items hain. A: cost ₹80,000, NRV ₹95,000. B: cost ₹60,000, NRV ₹42,000. C: cost ₹40,000, NRV ₹36,000. Lower of cost and NRV item-by-item lagao. Inventory kitni dikhegi, aur sab kuch cost par dikhane ke muqable profit kitna kam hoga?
questions.explanation: Item-wise: A = 80,000 (cost kam hai), B = 42,000, C = 36,000 ⇒ ₹1,58,000. Total cost 1,80,000 tha, to write-down = 22,000 (B ka 18,000 + C ka 4,000), aur profit utna kam. ₹1,73,000 total NRV hai — aggregate comparison A ke gain se B aur C ke loss ko chhupa deta hai; ₹1,62,000 sirf B ko adjust karta hai.

questions.question: Ek business ki opening Assets ₹5,00,000 aur Liabilities ₹1,50,000 hain. Saal me: (i) owner ne apni personal car (value ₹2,00,000) business ko capital ke roop me di, (ii) business account se owner ke bachche ki school fee ₹25,000 bhari gayi, (iii) ₹40,000 ki service cash me di, (iv) staff ki ₹18,000 salary outstanding hai. Saal ka profit aur closing equity kitne hain?
questions.explanation: Profit = service 40,000 − outstanding salary 18,000 = ₹22,000. Equity = 3,50,000 (opening) + 2,00,000 (car capital) − 25,000 (drawings) + 22,000 = ₹5,47,000. Car capital hai aur school fee drawings — dono equity badalte hain par profit nahi. −₹3,000 fee ko expense maanta hai, ₹2,22,000 car ko income, aur ₹40,000 / ₹5,65,000 outstanding salary bhool jaata hai.

weeks.title: Balance sheet and profit and loss: the building blocks
weeks.summary: Is week aap assets, liabilities, equity, income aur expenses ko sahi pehchanna seekhoge, balance sheet (ek date ki photo) aur statement of profit and loss (ek period ki film) ka fark samjhoge, aur capital vs revenue expenditure ka trap pakadna seekhoge.
concepts: **Asset**: aisa resource jo business control karta hai, kisi past event se mila hai, aur jisse future me economic benefit (cash) aane ki ummeed hai. Examples: cash, trade receivables (customers par baaki), inventory, machinery, building, patent. Employee ki skill asset nahi, kyunki business use control nahi karta aur measure bhi nahi kar sakta.

**Liability**: past event se bani present obligation, jise chukane me resources bahar jaayenge. Examples: trade payables (suppliers ko dena), bank loan, outstanding salary, customer se mila advance (goods dene ki obligation). Future me hone wala kharch (jaise agle saal ki salary) aaj liability nahi hai.

**Equity**: assets − liabilities, yaani owners ka residual claim. Sole proprietor me capital + profit − drawings; company me **share capital** + **reserves and surplus** (retained earnings yaani rakha hua profit). Equity koi alag cash ka dher nahi, bas claim ka hisaab hai.

**Income aur expenses**: income equity badhati hai (owners ke contribution ke alawa) — isme **revenue** (normal business se, jaise sales, fees) aur **gains** (side events se, jaise purani machine profit par bechna) dono aate hain. Expenses equity ghatate hain (drawings ke alawa) — salary, rent, electricity, depreciation, interest. Profit = Income − Expenses.

**Capital vs revenue expenditure**: jis kharch ka faayda kai saal milega (van, machine, building) wo **capital expenditure** hai — balance sheet me asset banta hai aur har saal depreciation ke roop me thoda-thoda expense hota hai. Rozmarra ka kharch (rent, salary, repairs) **revenue expenditure** hai — seedha P&L me. Loan ka principal chukana bhi expense nahi; sirf interest expense hai.

**Balance sheet vs statement of profit and loss**: balance sheet ek specific date ki position dikhata hai ('as at 31 March 2026') — photo jaisa. P&L ek period ki performance dikhata hai ('for the year ended 31 March 2026') — film jaisa. Dono ka link: saal ka profit equity (retained earnings) me judta hai.

**Classification ka shortcut**: khud se poochho — (1) kya ye cheez abhi bhi business ke paas hai aur future benefit degi? asset. (2) kya business ko kisi ko kuch dena hai? liability. (3) kya ye is period ka benefit use ho gaya? expense. (4) kya ye is period me kamaaya? income.

example.problem: Fictional coaching business 'Neel Tutorials' ke saal ke items: fees revenue ₹4,80,000; salaries ₹2,10,000; rent ₹72,000; electricity ₹18,000; depreciation ₹30,000; loan interest ₹12,000. Year-end par: equipment (net) ₹1,20,000; cash ₹95,000; fees receivable ₹40,000; bank loan ₹60,000; salaries payable ₹15,000. Owner ne saal me ₹1,00,000 capital daala aur ₹58,000 drawings kiye. Profit aur balance sheet banao.
steps: Check: 75,000 + 1,80,000 = 2,55,000. Answer: **profit ₹1,38,000, aur balance sheet ₹2,55,000 par balance hota hai**.
example.code:
Statement of profit and loss (year ended 31 March)
    Fees revenue                 4,80,000
    Less: total expenses        (3,42,000)
    Profit                       1,38,000

Balance sheet (as at 31 March)
    Equipment (net)              1,20,000
    Fees receivable                40,000
    Cash                           95,000
    Total assets                 2,55,000
    Capital + profit - drawings  1,80,000
    Bank loan                      60,000
    Salaries payable               15,000
    Total equity and liabilities 2,55,000

mistakes: Asset khareedne ka poora amount us saal ka expense likh dena. Van ₹3,00,000 ka hai to wo asset hai; P&L me sirf us saal ka depreciation jaata hai.
Loan repayment ko expense samajhna. Principal chukane se cash aur liability dono ghatte hain; P&L me sirf interest aata hai.
Kisi asset ki bikri par poori sale value ko revenue likhna. Normal business ke bahar ki sale par sirf gain/loss (sale price − carrying amount) P&L me jaata hai.
revision: Asset: control + past event + future benefit.
Liability: present obligation jisme resources bahar jaayenge.
Equity = Assets − Liabilities; Profit equity me judta hai.
Balance sheet = 'as at' date; P&L = 'for the year ended'.
Capital expenditure → asset (phir depreciation); revenue expenditure → seedha expense.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa item is mahine ka **expense** hai, asset nahi?
questions.explanation: Is mahine ki bijli ka benefit isi mahine use ho gaya, future benefit kuch nahi bacha, isliye expense. Machinery aur patent kai saal kaam aayenge (capital expenditure), aur inventory aage bikegi — teeno assets hain.

questions.question: Balance sheet aur statement of profit and loss ke baare me kaunsa statement sahi hai?
options: Balance sheet ek date ki position dikhata hai, P&L ek period ki performance
Balance sheet ek period ki performance dikhata hai, P&L ek date ki position
Dono ek hi date ki position dikhate hain, bas format alag hai
P&L me assets aur liabilities aate hain, balance sheet me revenue
questions.explanation: Balance sheet 'as at 31 March' ki photo hai — us din kya hai aur kya dena hai. P&L 'for the year ended 31 March' — poore saal kitna kamaaya aur kharch hua. Dusra option ulta hai aur sabse common confusion hai.

questions.question: Ek trading firm ke saal ke items: revenue ₹9,00,000; cost of goods sold ₹5,40,000; salaries ₹1,20,000; rent ₹60,000; nayi delivery van ki purchase ₹3,00,000; van par depreciation ₹30,000; bank loan ka principal repayment ₹50,000; loan interest ₹10,000. Saal ka profit kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Sirf expenses ghatao: 9,00,000 − 5,40,000 − 1,20,000 − 60,000 − 30,000 − 10,000 = ₹1,40,000. Van ki purchase capital expenditure hai (asset banta hai; P&L me sirf depreciation) aur principal repayment expense nahi. ₹90,000 repayment ghatane se aata hai, −₹1,30,000 van ko expense karne se, ₹1,70,000 depreciation bhoolne se.

questions.question: Ek company ke total assets ₹12,00,000 hain. Current liabilities ₹2,20,000, non-current liabilities ₹3,00,000, aur share capital ₹5,00,000 hai. Reserves and surplus kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: Total equity = 12,00,000 − 2,20,000 − 3,00,000 = 6,80,000. Isme share capital 5,00,000 hai, to reserves = ₹1,80,000. ₹6,80,000 poori equity hai (share capital ghatana bhool gaye), aur ₹4,80,000 / ₹4,00,000 ek type ki liability chhodne se aate hain.

questions.question: Ek bakery apna purana oven ₹85,000 me bechti hai. Bechne ke din oven ka carrying amount (cost − depreciation) ₹70,000 tha. Statement of profit and loss me kya dikhega?
options: Kuch nahi, sirf balance sheet badlegi
questions.explanation: Oven bechna bakery ka normal business nahi, isliye poora ₹85,000 revenue nahi. P&L me sirf gain = 85,000 − 70,000 = ₹15,000 (other income) aata hai. Sale price carrying amount se zyada hai, isliye loss nahi.

questions.question: Ek proprietor ki opening equity ₹4,00,000 thi. Saal me usne ₹1,00,000 extra capital daala aur ₹30,000 drawings kiye. Closing equity ₹5,20,000 hai. Saal ka profit kitna tha?
questions.explanation: Closing = Opening + capital introduced + profit − drawings ⇒ 5,20,000 = 4,00,000 + 1,00,000 + P − 30,000 ⇒ P = ₹50,000. ₹1,20,000 sirf equity ka badlav hai (naya capital profit nahi hota); ₹20,000 drawings ko wapas jodna bhoolne se aata hai; ₹1,50,000 naya capital ghatana bhoolne se.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa item 31 March ko business ki **liability** hai?
options: Customer se mila advance jiska maal abhi dena hai
Agle saal di jaane wali staff salary
questions.explanation: Advance lene se goods dene ki present obligation bani hai, isliye wo liability hai. Receivables aur inventory assets hain. Agle saal ki salary future ka kharch hai — kaam abhi hua nahi, to aaj koi obligation nahi; ye sabse common trap hai.

questions.question: Ek packaging unit ke in kharchon me se kaunsa **capital expenditure** hai?
options: Factory ke liye nayi packing machine khareedna
Office ka is mahine ka rent
questions.explanation: Nayi machine ka faayda kai saal milega, isliye wo asset banti hai aur har saal depreciation ke roop me expense hoti hai. Rent, salary aur routine servicing rozmarra ke kharch (revenue expenditure) hain — servicing machine se juda hone ke bawajood naya asset nahi banati.

questions.question: Ek salon ki saal ki service revenue ₹6,40,000 hai, aur purani chair bechne par ₹10,000 ka gain hua. Saal ke expenses ₹4,70,000 hain. Profit kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Income me revenue aur gains dono aate hain: 6,40,000 + 10,000 = 6,50,000. Profit = 6,50,000 − 4,70,000 = ₹1,80,000. ₹1,70,000 gain ko chhod deta hai, ₹1,60,000 gain ko ghata deta hai, aur ₹11,20,000 expenses ko jod deta hai.

questions.question: Ek trading business ke year-end items: cash ₹70,000; inventory ₹1,10,000; trade receivables ₹60,000; furniture ₹90,000; trade payables ₹80,000; bank loan ₹1,00,000; customer se mila advance ₹20,000. Owner ki equity kitni hai?
questions.explanation: Assets = 70,000 + 1,10,000 + 60,000 + 90,000 = 3,30,000. Liabilities = 80,000 + 1,00,000 + 20,000 = 2,00,000. Equity = ₹1,30,000. ₹1,50,000 advance ko liability nahi maanta, ₹1,70,000 use asset bana deta hai, aur ₹2,30,000 bank loan bhool jaata hai.

questions.question: Ek dukaan ke saal ke items: sales ₹7,50,000; cost of goods sold ₹4,20,000; rent ₹60,000; owner ki drawings ₹50,000; nayi machinery ki purchase ₹1,00,000; machinery par depreciation ₹20,000; loan interest ₹15,000. Saal ka profit kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Sirf expenses ghatao: 7,50,000 − 4,20,000 − 60,000 − 20,000 − 15,000 = ₹2,35,000. Drawings expense nahi (₹1,85,000 wala trap), machinery purchase capital expenditure hai (₹1,35,000 wala trap), aur depreciation bhoolne se ₹2,55,000 aata hai.

questions.question: Ek printing firm ne kuch saal pehle ₹2,40,000 ki machine khareedi thi; ab tak accumulated depreciation ₹1,50,000 hai. Wo machine ₹70,000 cash me bechi gayi. Is sale se pehle saal ka profit ₹3,00,000 tha. P&L me machine ki sale ka kya asar hai, aur final profit kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Carrying amount = 2,40,000 − 1,50,000 = 90,000. Sale 70,000 carrying se kam, to loss = ₹20,000; profit = 3,00,000 − 20,000 = ₹2,80,000. ₹70,000 gain poori sale value ko income maanta hai, 'gain ₹20,000' sign ulta karta hai, aur ₹1,70,000 loss depreciation ko ignore karke original cost se compare karta hai.

questions.question: Ek company ki opening share capital ₹10,00,000 aur reserves and surplus ₹3,00,000 thi. Saal me ₹2,00,000 ke naye shares face value par issue hue. Closing total assets ₹22,00,000 aur total liabilities ₹5,50,000 hain. Saal me koi dividend nahi diya gaya. Saal ka profit kitna tha?
questions.explanation: Closing equity = 22,00,000 − 5,50,000 = 16,50,000. Share capital ab 12,00,000 hai, to closing reserves = 4,50,000. Profit = 4,50,000 − 3,00,000 = ₹1,50,000. ₹3,50,000 poori equity ka badlav hai (naye shares profit nahi hote), ₹4,50,000 closing reserves hain, aur ₹6,50,000 naye shares ghatana bhool jaata hai.

questions.question: Ek proprietor ke year-end items: cash ₹50,000; customer se mila advance ₹30,000; patent ₹80,000; outstanding salary ₹25,000; trade receivables ₹70,000; bank loan ₹1,20,000; equipment ₹1,75,000. Saal ki shuruaat me capital ₹1,50,000 tha, saal me koi naya capital nahi aaya, aur drawings ₹40,000 the. Saal ka profit kitna tha?
questions.explanation: Assets = 50,000 + 80,000 + 70,000 + 1,75,000 = 3,75,000. Liabilities = 30,000 + 25,000 + 1,20,000 = 1,75,000. Equity = 2,00,000 = 1,50,000 + profit − 40,000 ⇒ profit = ₹90,000. ₹1,50,000 advance ko asset maan leta hai, ₹50,000 drawings ko bhool jaata hai, aur ₹10,000 drawings ko jodne ki jagah ghata deta hai.

questions.question: Ek proprietor ki opening equity ₹6,00,000 thi. Saal me: revenue ₹9,00,000; expenses ₹7,20,000; purani van bechne par gain ₹15,000; bank se ₹1,00,000 loan liya aur ₹50,000 chukaya; drawings ₹60,000. Closing equity kitni hai?
questions.explanation: Profit = 9,00,000 − 7,20,000 + 15,000 = 1,95,000. Closing equity = 6,00,000 + 1,95,000 − 60,000 = ₹7,35,000. Loan lena ya chukana sirf cash aur liability badalta hai, equity nahi — net ₹50,000 jodne se ₹7,85,000 aata hai. ₹7,20,000 gain bhool jaata hai aur ₹7,95,000 drawings.

weeks.title: How the statements connect: accruals, prepayments and deferrals
weeks.summary: Is week aap dekhoge ki balance sheet aur P&L ek doosre se kaise jude hain, aur year-end adjustments — prepaid expense, accrued expense, accrued income aur unearned revenue — kaise profit ko sahi period me laate hain.
concepts: **Link between statements**: P&L ka profit balance sheet me retained earnings (ya proprietor ke capital) me judta hai. Closing retained earnings = opening + profit − dividends. Isliye P&L ki har galti balance sheet ko bhi galat karti hai — dono statements ek hi double-entry se bante hain.

**Cash basis vs accrual basis**: cash basis me sirf paisa aane-jaane par record hota hai. Accrual basis (jo companies ke liye required hai) me revenue earn hone par aur expense incur hone par record hota hai. Fark timing ka hai: cash aur profit kisi saal alag ho sakte hain, par lambe time me barabar ho jaate hain.

**Prepaid expense (asset)**: paisa pehle de diya, benefit baad me milega. Jaise 1 Jan ko poore saal ka rent diya aur saal 31 March ko khatam hota hai — 3 mahine ka rent is saal ka expense, baaki 9 mahine ka **prepaid rent** current asset hai.

**Accrued expense (liability)**: benefit le liya, paisa baad me denge. March ki salary April me di to bhi March ka expense hai, aur 31 March ko **outstanding salary** liability hai. Isi tarah bijli, interest, wages.

**Accrued income (asset)**: kama liya, paisa abhi nahi aaya. Jaise FD ka interest jo is saal bana par bank ne abhi credit nahi kiya — revenue/income is saal ka, aur **interest receivable** asset. Trade receivables bhi isi family ke hain.

**Unearned (deferred) revenue (liability)**: paisa pehle aa gaya, kaam ya goods abhi dene hain. Annual subscription ka advance ek obligation hai; jaise-jaise mahine guzarte hain, liability ghatti hai aur revenue banta hai.

**Adjusting entries ka pattern**: har year-end adjustment ek P&L item aur ek balance sheet item ko chhoota hai — kabhi cash ko nahi (cash to pehle hi aa ya ja chuka hota hai). Prepaid aur accrued income profit badhate hain ya kam ghatate hain; accrued expense aur unearned revenue profit kam karte hain. Depreciation bhi ek adjustment hai: asset kam, expense zyada.
**Time-apportionment**: amount × (is period ke mahine ÷ total mahine). Mahine dhyaan se gino — 1 August se 31 March tak 8 mahine hain (Aug, Sep, Oct, Nov, Dec, Jan, Feb, Mar).

example.problem: Fictional firm 'Saanvi Coaching' (year end 31 March 2026) ka unadjusted profit ₹2,00,000 hai. Isme ye galtiyan hain: (a) 1 Oct 2025 ko diya gaya 12 mahine ka insurance ₹36,000 poora expense kiya gaya; (b) March ki salary ₹25,000 abhi record nahi hui (April me dene wale hain); (c) FD interest ₹4,000 jo is saal bana, record nahi hua; (d) March me mila ₹30,000 jo April–June ki classes ke liye hai, revenue me daal diya. Adjusted profit nikalo.
steps: (a) Insurance: Oct–Mar = 6 mahine is saal ke. Expense hona chahiye 36,000 × 6/12 = 18,000, par 36,000 kiya gaya. Prepaid ₹18,000 asset banao ⇒ profit +18,000.
(b) Outstanding salary ₹25,000: expense aur liability dono jodo ⇒ profit −25,000.
(c) Accrued interest ₹4,000: income aur receivable jodo ⇒ profit +4,000.
(d) Advance ₹30,000 abhi earn nahi hua: revenue se hatao, unearned revenue liability banao ⇒ profit −30,000.
Answer: **adjusted profit ₹1,67,000**; balance sheet me prepaid ₹18,000 aur interest receivable ₹4,000 assets, salary payable ₹25,000 aur unearned revenue ₹30,000 liabilities.

mistakes: Prepaid aur unearned ko ulta classify karna. Yaad rakho: humne pehle paisa diya ⇒ prepaid = asset; humne pehle paisa liya ⇒ unearned = liability.
Mahine galat ginna. 1 August se 31 March tak 8 mahine hain, 7 nahi — dono end-months shaamil karo agar period mahine ki 1 tarikh se shuru hota hai.
Adjustment me cash ko chhedna. Year-end adjustments sirf P&L aur balance sheet ke non-cash items badalte hain; cash already sahi hota hai.
revision: Prepaid expense = asset; accrued expense = liability.
Accrued income = asset; unearned revenue = liability.
Har adjustment: ek P&L item + ek balance sheet item, cash nahi.
Closing retained earnings = opening + profit − dividends.
Time-apportion: amount × months in period ÷ total months.

questions.question: Ek magazine publisher ko 31 March se pehle ₹1,20,000 ki subscriptions mil gayin, jinke issues agle saal bhejne hain. 31 March ki balance sheet me ye amount kya hai?
questions.explanation: Paisa aa gaya par magazines dene ki obligation baaki hai, isliye ye unearned revenue — ek liability. Ise is saal ka revenue maanna sabse common trap hai; revenue tab banega jab issues bheje jaayenge.

questions.question: Staff ne March me kaam kiya; unki ₹40,000 salary April me di jaayegi. Financial year 31 March ko khatam hota hai. Sahi treatment kya hai?
options: March ka expense ₹40,000, aur 31 March ko ₹40,000 liability
April ka expense, kyunki cash April me jaayega
Koi entry nahi, jab tak payment na ho
questions.explanation: Accrual concept: expense tab hota hai jab service use hui — March me. Paisa abhi nahi diya, isliye outstanding salary liability bhi banti hai. 'April ka expense' cash basis ki soch hai.

questions.question: Ek shop ne 1 January 2026 ko poore 12 mahine ka rent ₹1,20,000 advance me diya. Financial year 31 March 2026 ko khatam hota hai. 31 March 2026 ki balance sheet me prepaid rent kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: Jan–Mar = 3 mahine is saal ke: expense = 1,20,000 × 3/12 = 30,000. Baaki 9 mahine ka benefit aage milega: prepaid = 1,20,000 × 9/12 = ₹90,000. ₹30,000 is saal ka expense hai, prepaid nahi — ye dono ko ulta karne ka trap hai.

questions.question: Ek online learning startup ko 1 August 2025 ko ek customer se 12 mahine ke subscription ke ₹24,000 mile. Financial year 31 March 2026 ko khatam hota hai. Is financial year me kitna revenue recognise hoga?
questions.explanation: Aug se Mar tak 8 mahine service di: 24,000 × 8/12 = ₹16,000. Baaki ₹8,000 unearned revenue (liability) hai. ₹14,000 tab aata hai jab mahine 7 gin lete ho; ₹24,000 poora cash ko revenue maanne ka trap hai.

questions.question: Ek company March ka ₹12,000 ka electricity bill (payment April me) record karna bhool gayi. 31 March ke statements par iska kya asar hai?
options: Profit ₹12,000 zyada aur liabilities ₹12,000 kam dikhi
Profit ₹12,000 kam aur liabilities ₹12,000 zyada dikhi
Profit sahi hai, sirf cash galat hai
Profit ₹12,000 zyada aur assets ₹12,000 zyada dikhe
questions.explanation: Chhoota hua entry hai: expense ₹12,000 aur outstanding liability ₹12,000. Expense na hone se profit (aur equity) ₹12,000 zyada dikha, liability ₹12,000 kam. Cash par koi asar nahi, kyunki payment April me hai — 'sirf cash galat' wala option isi ko ulta samajhta hai.

questions.question: Ek firm ne saal me customers se ₹5,00,000 cash liya, jisme ₹40,000 pichhle saal ki sales ka tha. Saal ke end par is saal ki sales ke ₹60,000 abhi receivable hain. Expenses ke liye ₹3,20,000 cash diya, jisme ₹10,000 agle saal ka prepaid hai; aur ₹25,000 expenses abhi outstanding hain. Accrual basis par is saal ka profit kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Revenue = 5,00,000 − 40,000 (pichhle saal ka) + 60,000 (receivable) = 5,20,000. Expenses = 3,20,000 − 10,000 (prepaid) + 25,000 (outstanding) = 3,35,000. Profit = ₹1,85,000. ₹1,80,000 cash-basis answer hai; ₹2,25,000 pichhle saal ke ₹40,000 ko na hatane se; ₹1,65,000 prepaid ko ghatane ki jagah jodne se aata hai.

questions.question: 31 March ko ek company ke paas ₹18,000 ka prepaid insurance hai (agle saal ke mahinon ka premium pehle hi de diya). Balance sheet me ye kya hai?
questions.explanation: Paisa pehle diya aur benefit (insurance cover) aage milega, isliye prepaid ek current asset hai. Ise liability samajhna prepaid aur unearned ko ulta karne ka trap hai — liability tab hoti jab humne paisa liya hota aur kuch dena baaki hota.

questions.question: Ek company ki FD par is saal ₹6,000 interest bana, par bank ne abhi tak account me credit nahi kiya. Financial year 31 March ko khatam hota hai. Sahi treatment kya hai?
options: Koi entry nahi, jab tak bank credit na kare
questions.explanation: Accrued income: interest is saal kamaaya gaya, to income isi saal; paisa abhi aaya nahi, isliye interest receivable asset. 'Koi entry nahi' cash basis ki soch hai, aur liability galat hai kyunki company ko kuch dena nahi, lena hai.

questions.question: Ek firm ne 1 December 2025 ko 12 mahine ka insurance premium ₹24,000 diya. Financial year 31 March 2026 ko khatam hota hai. Is saal ka insurance expense kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Dec, Jan, Feb, Mar = 4 mahine is saal ke: 24,000 × 4/12 = ₹8,000. Baaki ₹16,000 prepaid asset hai, expense nahi. ₹6,000 sirf 3 mahine gin leta hai, aur ₹24,000 poore payment ko expense maanta hai.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa year-end adjustment profit ko **kam** karta hai?
options: Agle saal ka prepaid rent expense se hata kar asset banana
March ki outstanding wages record karna
Is saal ka accrued interest income record karna
Unearned revenue ka is saal earn hua hissa revenue me laana
questions.explanation: Outstanding wages ek naya expense (aur liability) jodti hain, isliye profit ghatta hai. Prepaid ko expense se hatana, accrued income record karna, aur unearned ka earn hua hissa revenue me laana — teeno profit badhate hain. Pattern: accrued expense aur unearned revenue (jab tak earn na ho) profit kam rakhte hain.

questions.question: Ek gym ne 1 November 2025 ko 1,000 members se 12 mahine ki membership ke ₹6,000 per member advance liye. Financial year 31 March 2026 ko khatam hota hai. 31 March 2026 ki balance sheet me unearned revenue kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: Total advance = 1,000 × 6,000 = 60,00,000. Nov–Mar = 5 mahine ki service di: earned = 60,00,000 × 5/12 = 25,00,000. Baaki 7 mahine = ₹35,00,000 liability. ₹25,00,000 is saal ka revenue hai (ulta karne ka trap), ₹60,00,000 kuch bhi earn nahi maanta, aur ₹30,00,000 mahine galat ginne se aata hai.

questions.question: Ek firm (year end 31 March 2026) ka unadjusted profit ₹3,50,000 hai. Galtiyan: (a) 1 September 2025 ko 12 mahine ka rent ₹48,000 diya, poora expense kiya gaya; (b) March ki wages ₹22,000 record nahi hui; (c) 1 February 2026 ko 3 mahine ki consulting fee ₹45,000 advance mili, poori revenue me daal di; (d) saal ka depreciation ₹18,000 record nahi hua. Adjusted profit kitna hai?
questions.explanation: (a) Sep–Mar = 7 mahine: expense 28,000, prepaid 20,000 ⇒ +20,000. (b) −22,000. (c) Feb, Mar earn hue = 30,000; April ka 15,000 unearned ⇒ −15,000. (d) −18,000. Total = 3,50,000 + 20,000 − 22,000 − 15,000 − 18,000 = ₹3,15,000. ₹3,19,000 rent ke 6 mahine ginta hai, ₹2,85,000 poora advance hata deta hai, aur ₹2,75,000 prepaid ko jodne ki jagah ghatata hai.

questions.question: Year-end par accountant ne do kaam nahi kiye: (i) ₹15,000 accrued interest income record nahi kiya, aur (ii) ₹9,000 ka prepaid insurance poora expense me hi rehne diya. In dono ka reported profit aur total assets par combined asar kya hai?
options: Profit ₹24,000 zyada aur assets ₹24,000 zyada dikhe
Profit ₹6,000 kam aur assets ₹6,000 kam dikhe
Profit ₹24,000 kam dikha, assets par asar nahi
Profit ₹24,000 kam aur assets ₹24,000 kam dikhe
questions.explanation: (i) Income aur receivable dono chhoote: profit −15,000, assets −15,000. (ii) Prepaid asset nahi bana aur expense zyada raha: profit −9,000, assets −9,000. Combined: dono ₹24,000 kam. ₹6,000 tab aata hai jab prepaid ko ulta (profit badhane wala) maan lete ho; 'assets par asar nahi' bhool jaata hai ki har adjustment ek balance sheet item ko bhi chhoota hai.

questions.question: Ek company ne saal me salary ke ₹9,60,000 cash me diye. Isme pichhle saal ki ₹70,000 outstanding salary bhi shaamil hai jo is saal chukayi gayi. Saal ke end par is saal ki ₹85,000 salary abhi outstanding hai. Accrual basis par is saal ka salary expense kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Expense = cash paid − pichhle saal ka hissa + is saal ka baaki = 9,60,000 − 70,000 + 85,000 = ₹9,75,000. ₹9,45,000 dono adjustments ke sign ulte karta hai, ₹9,60,000 seedha cash basis hai, aur ₹11,15,000 pichhle saal ka 70,000 ghatane ki jagah jod deta hai.

questions.question: Ek software firm ko do subscription advance mile: 1 July 2025 ko ₹36,000 (12 mahine ke liye) aur 1 January 2026 ko ₹18,000 (6 mahine ke liye). Financial year 31 March 2026 ko khatam hota hai. Is saal ka revenue aur 31 March ka unearned revenue kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Pehla: Jul–Mar = 9 mahine ⇒ 36,000 × 9/12 = 27,000 earned, 9,000 unearned. Doosra: Jan–Mar = 3 of 6 mahine ⇒ 18,000 × 3/6 = 9,000 earned, 9,000 unearned. Total: revenue ₹36,000, unearned ₹18,000. ₹54,000 poora cash revenue maanta hai; ₹33,000 pehle me 8 mahine ginta hai; ₹31,500 doosre ko 12 mahine par baant deta hai jabki wo 6 mahine ka hai.

weeks.title: Inventory, depreciation and contingent liabilities
weeks.summary: Is week aap FIFO aur weighted average se cost of goods sold aur closing inventory nikalna, straight line aur written-down value se depreciation lagana, aur provision vs contingent liability ka fark samajhna seekhoge.
concepts: **Cost of goods sold (COGS)**: COGS = opening inventory + purchases − closing inventory. Jo maal bika uska cost P&L me expense, jo bacha wo balance sheet me current asset. Isliye closing inventory ki value seedha profit ko badalti hai: closing inventory zyada ⇒ COGS kam ⇒ profit zyada.

**FIFO (first in, first out)**: maana jaata hai ki pehle khareeda maal pehle bikta hai. COGS me purane (pehle wale) rates lagte hain aur closing inventory me naye rates. Badhti keemat (rising prices) me FIFO se COGS kam, closing inventory aur profit zyada aate hain.

**Weighted average cost**: total available maal ka cost ÷ total units = average cost per unit; bike aur bache dono units isi rate par. Is course me periodic method use karenge (poore period ka ek average). Ind AS 2 me interchangeable (ek jaise) items ke liye sirf FIFO ya weighted average allowed hai (unique items, jaise custom machinery, ke liye specific identification) — **LIFO allowed nahi** hai. Simple average of prices (units ka weight liye bina) galat hai.

**Depreciation**: machine, building, vehicle jaise assets ka cost unki useful life par baantna (matching concept). Depreciable amount = cost − residual value. Land usually depreciate nahi hoti. Carrying amount (book value) = cost − accumulated depreciation. Depreciation ek non-cash expense hai.
**Straight line method (SLM)**: har saal barabar depreciation = (cost − residual value) ÷ useful life. Jaise ₹5,00,000 ki machine, residual ₹50,000, life 5 saal ⇒ ₹90,000 har saal.

**Written-down value (WDV) method**: har saal opening carrying amount par fixed rate. Shuru ke saalon me zyada, baad me kam depreciation. Rate 20% aur cost ₹5,00,000: saal 1 = 1,00,000, saal 2 = 4,00,000 × 20% = 80,000, saal 3 = 3,20,000 × 20% = 64,000. Rate kabhi cost par nahi lagta (wo SLM jaisa ban jaayega).

**Provision vs contingent liability (Ind AS 37)**: agar past event se present obligation hai, outflow **probable** hai aur amount reliably estimate ho sakta hai ⇒ **provision** recognise karo (expense + liability). Agar outflow sirf **possible** hai (ya reliably measure nahi hota) ⇒ **contingent liability**: balance sheet me nahi, sirf notes me disclose. Agar chance **remote** hai ⇒ kuch nahi. Ye conservatism ka practical roop hai.

example.problem: Fictional dukaan 'Kiran Footwear' ka data: opening 100 pairs @ ₹50; purchase 1: 200 pairs @ ₹55; purchase 2: 100 pairs @ ₹60. Period me 250 pairs bike. FIFO aur weighted average (periodic) dono se COGS aur closing inventory nikalo.
steps: Total available: 400 pairs, cost = 5,000 + 11,000 + 6,000 = ₹22,000. Closing units = 400 − 250 = 150.
FIFO COGS: pehle opening ke 100 × 50 = 5,000, phir purchase 1 ke 150 × 55 = 8,250 ⇒ COGS = ₹13,250.
Weighted average: 22,000 ÷ 400 = ₹55 per pair. COGS = 250 × 55 = ₹13,750; closing = 150 × 55 = ₹8,250.
Prices badh rahe the, isliye FIFO me COGS ₹500 kam aur profit ₹500 zyada.
Answer: **FIFO: COGS ₹13,250, closing ₹8,750; weighted average: COGS ₹13,750, closing ₹8,250**.

mistakes: WDV me har saal original cost par rate lagana. Rate hamesha us saal ke opening carrying amount par lagta hai, isliye depreciation har saal ghatta hai.
SLM me residual value ghatana bhool jaana. Depreciable amount = cost − residual value.
Weighted average me prices ka simple average lena. Units se weight do: total cost ÷ total units.
revision: COGS = opening inventory + purchases − closing inventory.
Rising prices: FIFO ⇒ kam COGS, zyada closing inventory aur profit.
Ind AS 2: FIFO ya weighted average; LIFO nahi.
SLM = (cost − residual) ÷ life; WDV = rate × opening carrying amount.
Probable + reliable estimate ⇒ provision; possible ⇒ disclose; remote ⇒ ignore.

questions.question: Saal bhar purchase prices lagataar badhti rahin. FIFO aur weighted average ki tulna me kaunsa statement sahi hai?
options: Weighted average se closing inventory zyada aur profit zyada aata hai
Dono methods se hamesha same profit aata hai
FIFO se closing inventory zyada aur profit zyada aata hai
FIFO se COGS zyada aur profit kam aata hai
questions.explanation: FIFO me purane, saste units pehle COGS me jaate hain aur naye, mehenge units closing inventory me bachte hain. Isliye rising prices me FIFO ka COGS kam aur profit zyada hota hai. Aakhri option tab sahi hota jab prices gir rahi hoti.

questions.question: Opening inventory 50 units @ ₹200, purchase 1: 150 units @ ₹220, purchase 2: 100 units @ ₹250. Period me 220 units bike. FIFO se cost of goods sold kitna hai?
questions.explanation: FIFO: 50 × 200 = 10,000; 150 × 220 = 33,000; baaki 20 × 250 = 5,000 ⇒ COGS = ₹48,000 (closing = 80 × 250 = 20,000). ₹49,867 weighted average hai (68,000 ÷ 300 × 220), ₹51,400 LIFO (naye units pehle) hai jo Ind AS me allowed nahi, aur ₹44,000 sab units ko ₹200 par lene ka trap hai.

questions.question: Opening 40 units @ ₹100 aur purchase 60 units @ ₹110. 70 units bike. Weighted average (periodic) method se closing inventory ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: Average = (4,000 + 6,600) ÷ 100 = ₹106 per unit. Closing 30 units × 106 = ₹3,180. ₹3,150 prices ka simple average (105) lene se aata hai — units ka weight bhool gaye; ₹3,300 FIFO aur ₹3,000 LIFO answer hai.

questions.question: Ek machine ₹5,00,000 me khareedi gayi; useful life 5 saal, residual value ₹50,000. Straight line method se 2 saal baad carrying amount kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: Annual depreciation = (5,00,000 − 50,000) ÷ 5 = 90,000. Do saal ka 1,80,000 ⇒ carrying amount = ₹3,20,000. ₹3,00,000 residual value ignore karne se (1,00,000 per year) aata hai.

questions.question: ₹5,00,000 ki ek delivery van par written-down value method se 20% depreciation lagta hai. Teesre saal ka depreciation kitna hoga?

Year-end par ek company par teen court cases hain. Case A: ₹4,00,000, lawyers ke hisaab se haarna probable hai aur amount reliable hai. Case B: ₹6,00,000, haarna sirf possible hai. Case C: ₹2,00,000, haarne ka chance remote hai. Ind AS 37 ke hisaab se kitna provision banega aur kitna contingent liability ke roop me disclose hoga?
questions.explanation: A probable aur measurable hai ⇒ ₹4,00,000 provision (expense + liability). B possible hai ⇒ ₹6,00,000 sirf notes me contingent liability. C remote hai ⇒ disclose bhi nahi. ₹8,00,000 disclose karna remote case ko bhi shaamil karne ka trap hai; ₹10,00,000 provision possible ko probable samajhne se aata hai.

questions.question: Ek dukaan ki opening inventory ₹40,000, saal ki purchases ₹2,10,000 aur closing inventory ₹55,000 hai. Cost of goods sold kitna hai?
questions.explanation: COGS = opening + purchases − closing = 40,000 + 2,10,000 − 55,000 = ₹1,95,000. ₹2,25,000 opening aur closing ko ulta laga deta hai, ₹1,55,000 opening inventory bhool jaata hai, aur ₹3,05,000 closing ko ghatane ki jagah jod deta hai.

questions.question: Ind AS 2 ke hisaab se interchangeable (ek jaise) inventory items ki costing ke baare me kaunsa statement sahi hai?
options: LIFO aur FIFO allowed hain, weighted average nahi
Purchase prices ka simple average sabse sahi method hai
LIFO allowed nahi; FIFO ya weighted average use karna hoga
questions.explanation: Ind AS 2 me interchangeable items ke liye FIFO ya weighted average cost hi allowed hai, LIFO nahi. Specific identification unique items (jaise custom machinery) ke liye hai. Simple average galat hai kyunki wo units ka weight nahi leta.

questions.question: Ek company ke in assets me se kis par usually depreciation **nahi** lagta?
questions.explanation: Land ki useful life aam taur par khatam nahi hoti, isliye usually depreciate nahi hoti. Building, van aur computers time aur use ke saath ghiste hain, to unka cost useful life par baanta jaata hai. Building aur land ko ek jaisa maan lena common trap hai.

questions.question: Ek studio ne ₹1,80,000 ka printer khareeda; residual value ₹20,000 aur useful life 4 saal hai. Straight line method se har saal ka depreciation kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: Depreciable amount = 1,80,000 − 20,000 = 1,60,000; har saal = 1,60,000 ÷ 4 = ₹40,000. ₹45,000 residual value ghatana bhool jaata hai, ₹50,000 residual ko jod deta hai, aur ₹1,60,000 poora depreciable amount ek hi saal me daal deta hai.

questions.question: Ek customer ne company par ₹5,00,000 ka case kiya hai. Lawyers ke hisaab se company ka haarna possible hai, par probable nahi. Ind AS 37 ke hisaab se year-end par kya hoga?
options: Provision nahi; contingent liability ke roop me notes me disclose
Kuch nahi — na provision, na disclosure
₹2,50,000 provision aur baaki notes me disclose
questions.explanation: Outflow sirf possible hai, probable nahi, isliye provision nahi banega; par chance remote bhi nahi, to contingent liability ke roop me notes me disclose hoga. Poora provision tab banta jab haarna probable hota; 'kuch nahi' sirf remote case ke liye hai; aadha provision koi rule nahi.

questions.question: Opening inventory 200 units @ ₹30; purchase 1: 300 units @ ₹34; purchase 2: 250 units @ ₹38. Period me 600 units ₹50 per unit par bike. FIFO se gross profit aur closing inventory kitne hain?
questions.explanation: FIFO COGS = 200 × 30 + 300 × 34 + 100 × 38 = 6,000 + 10,200 + 3,800 = 20,000. Revenue = 600 × 50 = 30,000 ⇒ GP ₹10,000. Closing = 150 × 38 = ₹5,700. ₹8,800 / ₹4,500 LIFO ki tarah naye units pehle bechta hai (Ind AS 2 me allowed nahi); ₹9,440 / ₹5,140 weighted average (25,700 ÷ 750) hai, FIFO nahi; ₹9,600 / ₹5,100 prices ka simple average ₹34 leta hai.

questions.question: Ek company ₹8,00,000 ki machine ke liye do methods compare kar rahi hai. Option 1: SLM, residual value ₹80,000, life 6 saal. Option 2: WDV 25%. Pehle 2 saal ka total depreciation dono methods me kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: SLM: (8,00,000 − 80,000) ÷ 6 = 1,20,000 per saal ⇒ 2 saal = ₹2,40,000. WDV: saal 1 = 8,00,000 × 25% = 2,00,000; saal 2 = 6,00,000 × 25% = 1,50,000 ⇒ ₹3,50,000. ₹2,66,667 SLM me residual bhool jaata hai; ₹4,00,000 WDV ka rate har saal cost par lagata hai; ₹3,15,000 WDV me pehle residual ghata deta hai, jo WDV me nahi hota.

questions.question: Year-end stock count me galti se closing inventory ₹1,20,000 ki jagah ₹1,50,000 count ho gayi, aur galti pakdi nahi gayi. Is saal ke profit aur agle saal ke profit par kya asar hoga?
options: Is saal ₹30,000 kam, agle saal ₹30,000 zyada
Is saal ₹30,000 zyada, agle saal par asar nahi
Sirf balance sheet galat, profit par asar nahi
Is saal ₹30,000 zyada, agle saal ₹30,000 kam
questions.explanation: COGS = opening + purchases − closing. Closing 30,000 zyada ⇒ is saal COGS 30,000 kam ⇒ profit ₹30,000 zyada. Yahi closing agle saal ki opening banti hai ⇒ agle saal COGS 30,000 zyada ⇒ profit ₹30,000 kam. 'Agle saal par asar nahi' bhool jaata hai ki closing hi next opening hai; aur closing inventory seedha profit badalti hai, sirf balance sheet nahi.

questions.question: Year-end par (in items se pehle) company ka PBT ₹20,00,000 hai. Items: (A) warranty claims ₹3,00,000 — outflow probable, estimate reliable; (B) supplier ka ₹5,00,000 claim — sirf possible; (C) ₹2,50,000 ka tax dispute — outflow probable, par amount reliably estimate nahi ho sakta; (D) ₹1,00,000 ka case — chance remote. Ind AS 37 ke baad PBT kitna hoga aur notes me contingent liability kitni disclose hogi?
questions.explanation: Provision sirf A ka (probable + reliable): PBT = 20,00,000 − 3,00,000 = ₹17,00,000. B possible hai aur C reliably measure nahi hota — dono contingent liabilities: 5,00,000 + 2,50,000 = ₹7,50,000. D remote, kuch nahi. ₹14,50,000 C ka bhi provision bana deta hai, ₹8,50,000 remote case ko bhi disclose karta hai, aur ₹9,50,000 A, B, C teeno ka provision bana deta hai.

weeks.title: Tax, dividends and the double-entry idea
weeks.summary: Is week aap profit before tax se profit after tax tak pahunchna, dividend ko expense nahi balki profit ka distribution samajhna, aur double entry ka dual-aspect logic seekhoge jisse har transaction do jagah record hota hai.
concepts: **Income tax expense**: company apne taxable profit par income tax deti hai. P&L me order: Profit before tax (PBT) − tax expense = **Profit after tax (PAT)**. Is course ke sawalon me hum simple flat rate (jaise 25%) maanenge; real life me taxable profit Income-tax Act ke rules se nikalta hai aur accounting profit se alag ho sakta hai.

**Tax expense vs tax paid**: P&L ka tax expense accrual basis par hai. Company saal me advance tax bharti hai; year-end par expense − advance tax = **current tax liability (tax payable)**. Jaise expense ₹2,00,000 aur advance tax ₹1,50,000 ⇒ ₹50,000 payable.

**Deferred tax (sirf idea)**: jab kisi item ka accounting aur tax treatment alag timing par hota hai (jaise tax rules me depreciation jaldi milna), to future me tax ka farak **deferred tax liability ya asset** ke roop me dikhaya jaata hai. Abhi bas itna yaad rakho ki tax expense = current tax + deferred tax.

**Dividend**: PAT ka wo hissa jo equity shareholders ko baanta jaata hai. Ye **expense nahi** hai — P&L ke baad retained earnings se ghatta hai (statement of changes in equity me dikhta hai). Interim dividend board deta hai; final dividend AGM me shareholders approve karte hain. Ind AS me dividend tab liability banta hai jab wo properly declare ho jaata hai (interim: board ka decision; final: shareholders ka approval); year-end ke baad propose hua final dividend sirf notes me disclose hota hai.

**Dividend metrics**: dividend per share (DPS) = total dividend ÷ number of equity shares. **Payout ratio** = dividend ÷ PAT; retention ratio = 1 − payout. India me 1 April 2020 se dividend shareholder ke haath me taxable hai (dividend distribution tax hata diya gaya).

**Double entry / dual aspect**: har transaction kam se kam do accounts ko chhoota hai, aur dono taraf barabar amount — isliye Assets = Liabilities + Equity kabhi nahi bigadta. Char common patterns: asset ↑ liability ↑ (credit par maal), asset ↑ asset ↓ (cash se machine), asset ↓ liability ↓ (creditor ko payment), asset ↑ equity ↑ (revenue ya capital).

**Debit aur credit ki shuruaat**: har account ke do side hote hain — left = **debit (Dr)**, right = **credit (Cr)**. Assets aur expenses badhne par debit; liabilities, equity aur revenue badhne par credit. Har entry me total debit = total credit. Poore rules, journal aur ledger week 8 me detail me aayenge.

example.problem: Fictional company 'Tara Textiles Ltd' ka PBT ₹8,00,000 hai, tax rate 25%. Saal me ₹1,50,000 advance tax bhara. Board ne 1,00,000 equity shares par ₹2 per share dividend diya (approved aur paid). Opening retained earnings ₹3,00,000 thi. PAT, tax payable, payout ratio aur closing retained earnings nikalo.
steps: Dividend = 1,00,000 × ₹2 = ₹2,00,000. Ye P&L me nahi jaata, retained earnings se ghatta hai.
Answer: **PAT ₹6,00,000, tax payable ₹50,000, payout 33.3%, closing retained earnings ₹7,00,000**.

mistakes: Dividend ko P&L me expense ki tarah ghatana. Dividend PAT ke baad, retained earnings se ghatta hai; PAT par iska koi asar nahi.
Payout ratio me PBT se divide karna. Shareholders ka hissa tax ke baad ka profit hai, isliye dividend ÷ PAT.
Ek hi transaction ka sirf ek side record karna (jaise credit purchase me inventory badhayi par payable nahi). Har entry me debit = credit check karo.
revision: PAT = PBT − tax expense.
Tax payable = tax expense − advance tax paid.
Dividend: expense nahi, retained earnings se distribution.
Payout = dividend ÷ PAT; DPS = dividend ÷ shares.
Dual aspect: har transaction do jagah, Dr = Cr.

questions.question: Ek company ka profit before tax ₹12,00,000 hai aur tax rate 25% hai. Profit after tax kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: Tax = 12,00,000 × 25% = 3,00,000; PAT = 12,00,000 − 3,00,000 = ₹9,00,000. ₹3,00,000 sirf tax hai, aur ₹15,00,000 tax ko ghatane ki jagah jodne ka trap hai.

questions.question: Equity shareholders ko diye gaye dividend ke baare me kaunsa statement sahi hai?
options: Ye P&L me expense hai aur PAT ko kam karta hai
Ye saal ki shuruaat me hi liability ban jaata hai
Ye retained earnings ko badhata hai
Ye profit ka distribution hai jo retained earnings ko kam karta hai
questions.explanation: Dividend profit kamaane ka kharch nahi, kamaaye hue profit ko owners me baantna hai. Isliye PAT ke baad retained earnings se ghatta hai. Pehla option sabse common trap hai — dividend se PAT nahi badalta.

questions.question: Ek company ki opening retained earnings ₹5,00,000 hai. Is saal PAT ₹3,00,000 hai aur 80,000 equity shares par ₹1.5 per share dividend diya gaya. Closing retained earnings kitni hongi?
questions.explanation: Dividend = 80,000 × 1.5 = 1,20,000. Closing = 5,00,000 + 3,00,000 − 1,20,000 = ₹6,80,000. ₹8,00,000 dividend bhoolne se, ₹1,80,000 opening balance bhoolne se, aur ₹9,20,000 dividend ko jodne se aata hai.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa transaction business ke **total assets** ko nahi badalta?
questions.explanation: Cash se machinery: ek asset (machinery) badha, doosra (cash) utna hi ghata — total same. Loan aur capital se assets badhte hain; creditor ko payment se cash aur liability dono ghatte hain, to total assets kam ho jaate hain.

questions.question: Ek company ka PBT ₹10,00,000 hai, tax rate 25%, aur saal me ₹3,00,000 dividend diya gaya. Dividend payout ratio kya hai?
questions.explanation: PAT = 10,00,000 × 75% = 7,50,000. Payout = 3,00,000 ÷ 7,50,000 = 40%. 30% tab aata hai jab PBT se divide karte ho; 60% retention ratio hai, payout nahi.

questions.question: Ek business ke Assets ₹6,00,000 = Liabilities ₹2,00,000 + Equity ₹4,00,000 hain. Phir: (a) ₹50,000 ki inventory credit par khareedi, (b) supplier ko ₹20,000 cash diye, (c) ₹30,000 cost wali inventory ₹45,000 cash me bechi. Ab total assets kitne hain?
questions.explanation: (a) inventory +50,000, payables +50,000. (b) cash −20,000, payables −20,000. (c) cash +45,000, inventory −30,000, equity +15,000. Assets = 6,00,000 + 50,000 − 20,000 + 45,000 − 30,000 = ₹6,45,000 = liabilities 2,30,000 + equity 4,15,000. ₹6,75,000 bechi gayi inventory hatana bhoolne se aata hai; ₹6,65,000 supplier payment ka cash ghatana bhoolne se.

questions.question: Ek company ka is saal ka income tax expense ₹3,60,000 hai, aur usne saal me ₹2,80,000 advance tax bhara. Year-end par current tax liability (tax payable) kitni hogi?
questions.explanation: Tax payable = tax expense − advance tax = 3,60,000 − 2,80,000 = ₹80,000. ₹3,60,000 advance tax ko bhool jaata hai, ₹2,80,000 wo hai jo bhara ja chuka, aur ₹6,40,000 dono ko jod deta hai.

questions.question: Ek company ne 2,40,000 equity shares par kul ₹6,00,000 dividend diya. Dividend per share (DPS) kitna hai?
questions.explanation: DPS = total dividend ÷ number of shares = 6,00,000 ÷ 2,40,000 = ₹2.50. ₹0.40 ulta divide karne (shares ÷ dividend) se aata hai, ₹25.00 decimal galat lagane se, aur ₹1.25 answer ko bina wajah aadha kar deta hai.

questions.question: Debit-credit rules ke hisaab se inme se kis account ka **increase** debit side me record hota hai?
questions.explanation: Assets aur expenses badhne par debit hota hai, isliye rent expense ka increase debit hai. Bank loan (liability), share capital (equity) aur sales (revenue) badhne par credit hote hain. Revenue ko bhi 'P&L item' maan kar debit kar dena common galti hai.

questions.question: Ek company ka PAT ₹16,00,000 hai. Isme se ₹12,00,000 retained kiya gaya aur baaki equity shareholders ko dividend diya gaya. Company ke 4,00,000 equity shares hain. Payout ratio aur DPS kya hain?
questions.explanation: Dividend = 16,00,000 − 12,00,000 = 4,00,000. Payout = 4,00,000 ÷ 16,00,000 = 25%; DPS = 4,00,000 ÷ 4,00,000 = ₹1.00. 75% / ₹3.00 retained amount ko dividend maan leta hai, ₹4.00 PAT ko shares se divide karta hai (wo EPS hai), aur 33.3% dividend ko retained amount se divide karta hai, PAT se nahi.

questions.question: Ek customer ko pichhle mahine credit par maal becha gaya tha. Aaj usne ₹25,000 cash me chuka diye. Accounting equation par is transaction ka kya asar hai?
options: Ek asset badha aur doosra asset utna hi ghata; total same
questions.explanation: Cash +25,000 aur trade receivables −25,000 — sirf assets ki shakal badli (asset ↑ asset ↓). Revenue to sale ke din record ho chuka tha, isliye equity dobara nahi badhti — 'equity badhi' wala option sale ko double count karta hai. Liabilities is transaction me kahin nahi hain.

questions.question: Ek company ka PBT ₹20,00,000 hai, tax rate 25%, aur 5,00,000 equity shares hain. Saal me board ne ₹1 per share interim dividend declare karke pay kiya. Year-end (31 March) ke baad board ne ₹2 per share final dividend propose kiya, jo AGM me baad me approve hoga. Opening retained earnings ₹8,00,000 thi. 31 March ki closing retained earnings kitni hongi?
questions.explanation: PAT = 20,00,000 − 25% = 15,00,000. Interim dividend = 5,00,000 × ₹1 = 5,00,000. Closing RE = 8,00,000 + 15,00,000 − 5,00,000 = ₹18,00,000. Year-end ke baad propose hua final dividend abhi liability nahi, sirf notes me disclose hota hai. ₹8,00,000 final dividend bhi ghata deta hai, ₹23,00,000 interim bhi bhool jaata hai, aur ₹13,00,000 interim ki jagah final ghatata hai.

questions.question: Ek company ki opening tax payable ₹40,000 thi (pichhle saal ki, jo is saal bhar di gayi). Is saal PBT ₹12,00,000 hai aur tax rate 25%. Is saal ke liye ₹2,50,000 advance tax bhara gaya. Year-end par closing tax payable kitni hogi?
questions.explanation: Is saal ka tax expense = 12,00,000 × 25% = 3,00,000. Pichhle saal ka 40,000 chuk gaya, to wo khatam. Closing payable = 3,00,000 − 2,50,000 = ₹50,000. ₹90,000 opening 40,000 ko abhi bhi baaki maanta hai, ₹3,00,000 advance tax bhool jaata hai, aur ₹10,000 opening ko is saal ke tax se ek baar aur ghata deta hai.

questions.question: Ek company ki shuruaat me Assets ₹50,00,000 = Liabilities ₹20,00,000 + Equity ₹30,00,000 hai. Saal ka PBT ₹8,00,000 hai (saara cash me mila). Tax rate 25%: isme se ₹1,50,000 advance tax bhara, baaki year-end par payable hai. ₹2,00,000 dividend declare karke pay kiya gaya. Year-end par total liabilities aur equity kitne hain?
questions.explanation: Tax expense = 2,00,000, PAT = 6,00,000. Tax payable = 2,00,000 − 1,50,000 = 50,000 ⇒ liabilities ₹20,50,000. Equity = 30,00,000 + 6,00,000 − 2,00,000 = ₹34,00,000. Check: assets = 50,00,000 + 8,00,000 − 1,50,000 − 2,00,000 = 54,50,000 = 20,50,000 + 34,00,000. ₹34,50,000 sirf bhare gaye tax ko expense maanta hai; ₹36,00,000 dividend ghatana bhool jaata hai; ₹36,50,000 dono galtiyan karta hai.

questions.question: Ek company ka PBT ₹24,00,000 hai aur tax rate 25%. Company ka retention ratio 60% hai, aur uske 3,00,000 equity shares hain. Dividend per share kitna hai?
questions.explanation: PAT = 24,00,000 × 75% = 18,00,000. Payout = 1 − 60% = 40% ⇒ dividend = 7,20,000. DPS = 7,20,000 ÷ 3,00,000 = ₹2.40. ₹3.60 retention ko payout maan leta hai, ₹3.20 payout ko PBT par lagata hai (PAT par lagna chahiye), aur ₹4.80 dono galtiyan saath karta hai.

weeks.title: Reading an annual report: the balance sheet
weeks.summary: Is week aap ek Indian company ke annual report ka balance sheet padhna seekhoge — Schedule III format, current vs non-current classification, share capital aur other equity (reserves), working capital aur book value per share.
concepts: **Annual report** me kya hota hai: directors' report, management discussion and analysis (MD&A), auditor's report, aur financial statements — balance sheet, statement of profit and loss, cash flow statement, statement of changes in equity, aur **notes** (jahan har line ka breakup aur accounting policies hoti hain). Numbers aksar '₹ in lakhs' ya '₹ in crores' me hote hain, aur saath me pichhle saal ka comparative column.

**Standalone vs consolidated**: standalone sirf company ke apne numbers dikhata hai. Consolidated statements parent aur uski subsidiaries ko ek group ki tarah jodte hain (aapas ke transactions hata kar). Group ki asli picture ke liye consolidated padho.

**Schedule III format** (Companies Act, 2013) vertical hai: pehle Assets (non-current, phir current), phir Equity and Liabilities (equity, non-current liabilities, current liabilities). Dono totals barabar hone chahiye.

**Current vs non-current**: jo asset 12 mahine (ya company ke normal operating cycle) ke andar cash me badalne ki ummeed hai, ya jo liability is period me chukani hai, wo **current**; baaki **non-current**. Long-term loan ki jo instalment agle 12 mahine me deni hai, wo current maturity hai aur current liabilities me (Schedule III me short-term borrowings ke andar) jaati hai.

**Typical lines**: non-current assets — property, plant and equipment (PPE), capital work-in-progress (adhoori construction), intangible assets, non-current investments. Current assets — inventories, trade receivables, cash and cash equivalents, other current assets (prepaid). Current liabilities — trade payables, short-term borrowings, other current liabilities (customer advances, statutory dues), current tax liabilities.

**Equity ka breakup**: equity share capital = shares × **face value**. Shares face value se zyada par issue hon to extra amount **securities premium** me jaata hai — ye other equity (reserve) hai, income nahi. Other equity me general reserve aur retained earnings bhi aate hain. **Book value per share** = total equity ÷ number of shares.

**Working capital** = current assets − current liabilities. Positive working capital short-term obligations ke liye buffer hai, par bahut zyada working capital ka matlab inventory ya receivables me paisa phansa hona bhi ho sakta hai. Ise hamesha business ki nature ke saath padho.

example.problem: Fictional company 'Prakash Pumps Ltd' ke balance sheet se (code block dekho) total check karo, working capital aur book value per share nikalo. Company ke 1,00,000 equity shares (face value ₹10) hain.
steps: Equity and liabilities = 24,00,000 + 8,00,000 + 9,00,000 = 41,00,000 — dono side barabar.
Working capital = 16,00,000 − 9,00,000 = ₹7,00,000. Long-term borrowings isme nahi aate.
Book value per share = 24,00,000 ÷ 1,00,000 = ₹24, jabki face value sirf ₹10 hai — farq reserves ki wajah se hai.
Answer: **working capital ₹7,00,000 aur book value per share ₹24**.
example.code:
Prakash Pumps Ltd - Balance sheet as at 31 March (in Rs)
ASSETS
  Non-current: PPE 20,00,000 | Capital WIP 3,00,000 | Investments 2,00,000
  Current:     Inventories 7,00,000 | Trade receivables 6,00,000
               Cash 2,50,000 | Other current assets 50,000
EQUITY AND LIABILITIES
  Equity:      Equity share capital 10,00,000 | Other equity 14,00,000
  Non-current: Long-term borrowings 8,00,000
  Current:     Trade payables 5,00,000 | Short-term borrowings 3,00,000
               Other current liabilities 1,00,000

mistakes: Long-term loan ki agle saal wali instalment ko bhi non-current me rakhna. Jo hissa 12 mahine me chukana hai wo current liability hai.
Securities premium ko P&L ki income samajhna. Ye shareholders ka extra capital hai aur other equity me jaata hai.
Face value ko share ki value maan lena. Book value = equity ÷ shares, aur market price in dono se alag ho sakta hai.
revision: Current = 12 mahine / operating cycle ke andar; baaki non-current.
Working capital = current assets − current liabilities.
Share capital = shares × face value; extra = securities premium.
Book value per share = total equity ÷ shares.
Consolidated = parent + subsidiaries ek group ki tarah.

questions.question: Ek manufacturing company ke balance sheet me inme se kaunsa item **current asset** hoga?
options: Doosri company ke shares me long-term investment
questions.explanation: Inventory normal operating cycle me bik kar cash ban jaati hai, isliye current asset hai. Land aur goodwill saalon tak rehte hain, aur long-term investment bhi lambe samay ke liye rakha gaya hai — teeno non-current.

questions.question: Ek company ke items: inventories ₹3,00,000; trade receivables ₹2,50,000; cash ₹1,00,000; prepaid expenses ₹20,000; trade payables ₹2,80,000; short-term borrowings ₹1,20,000; long-term borrowings ₹5,00,000; PPE ₹9,00,000. Working capital kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Current assets = 3,00,000 + 2,50,000 + 1,00,000 + 20,000 = 6,70,000. Current liabilities = 2,80,000 + 1,20,000 = 4,00,000. WC = ₹2,70,000. −₹2,30,000 long-term borrowings ko bhi current maanne se aata hai; ₹2,50,000 prepaid chhodne se; ₹3,90,000 short-term borrowings chhodne se.

questions.question: Ek company ne 50,000 equity shares (face value ₹10) ₹60 per share par issue kiye aur poora paisa mil gaya. Securities premium me kitna jaayega?
options: ₹0 — premium P&L me income ban jaata hai
questions.explanation: Har share par premium = 60 − 10 = ₹50; total = 50,000 × 50 = ₹25,00,000 (other equity). Share capital = 50,000 × 10 = 5,00,000, aur total cash 30,00,000. Premium shareholders ka capital hai, income nahi — isliye aakhri option galat hai.

questions.question: Annual report me 'consolidated balance sheet' kya dikhata hai?
options: Sirf parent company ke apne assets aur liabilities
Pichhle paanch saal ke balance sheets ka total
Parent aur uski subsidiaries ko ek group ki tarah jod kar
Sirf subsidiaries ke numbers, parent ke bina
questions.explanation: Consolidated statements parent aur subsidiaries ko ek economic entity maan kar jodte hain (aapas ke transactions hata kar). Sirf parent ke numbers standalone statements me hote hain — pehla option standalone ki definition hai.

questions.question: 31 March ko ek company par ₹10,00,000 ka term loan hai, jo ₹2,00,000 ki saalana instalments me chukana hai; pehli instalment agle 12 mahine me due hai. Balance sheet me ise kaise dikhayenge?
questions.explanation: Jo hissa agle 12 mahine me chukana hai (₹2,00,000) wo current maturity hai — current liabilities me. Baaki ₹8,00,000 non-current borrowings. Poora loan non-current dikhana sabse common galti hai, isse working capital zyada dikhta hai.

questions.question: Ek company ke total assets ₹50,00,000, non-current liabilities ₹15,00,000 aur current liabilities ₹9,00,000 hain. Uske 1,50,000 equity shares (face value ₹10) hain. Book value per share kitni hai?
questions.explanation: Total equity = 50,00,000 − 15,00,000 − 9,00,000 = 26,00,000 (share capital 15,00,000 + other equity 11,00,000). Book value = 26,00,000 ÷ 1,50,000 = ₹17.33. ₹33.33 total assets ko shares se divide karne ka trap hai (liabilities owners ki nahi); ₹10 face value hai; ₹7.33 sirf other equity per share hai.

questions.question: Annual report ke balance sheet me 'capital work-in-progress' kya dikhata hai?
options: Factory me adhoore bane goods — current asset
Employees ka bakaya kaam ka paisa — current liability
Ban rahi factory ya plant jo abhi use me nahi aaya — non-current asset
Share capital ka wo hissa jo abhi aana baaki hai
questions.explanation: Capital work-in-progress adhoori construction hai — jaise ban rahi building ya install ho rahi machinery — jo poori hone par PPE me jaayegi, isliye non-current asset. Adhoore goods 'work-in-progress inventory' hain jo inventories (current asset) me aate hain; naam milta-julta hone se ye common confusion hai.

questions.question: Ek company ki total equity ₹36,00,000 hai, aur uske 3,00,000 equity shares (face value ₹10) hain. Book value per share kitni hai?
questions.explanation: Book value per share = total equity ÷ shares = 36,00,000 ÷ 3,00,000 = ₹12. ₹10 sirf face value hai, ₹2 face value ke upar ka hissa (reserves per share) hai, aur ₹120 zero galat lagane se aata hai.

questions.question: Ek company ke balance sheet me inme se kaunsa item **current liability** hoga?
options: Debenture loan jo 10 saal baad chukana hai (agle 12 mahine me koi instalment nahi)
Customers se mile advances, jinka maal agle 3 mahine me dena hai
questions.explanation: Customer advances ki obligation agle 12 mahine me poori karni hai, isliye current liability (other current liabilities). Debenture jiski koi instalment agle 12 mahine me nahi, non-current hai. Securities premium other equity hai, aur CWIP ek non-current asset.

questions.question: Ek company ke equity items: equity share capital ₹10,00,000; securities premium ₹6,00,000; general reserve ₹3,00,000; retained earnings ₹5,00,000. Schedule III ke hisaab se 'other equity' aur total equity kitni hai?
questions.explanation: Other equity = securities premium + general reserve + retained earnings = 6,00,000 + 3,00,000 + 5,00,000 = 14,00,000. Total equity = 10,00,000 + 14,00,000 = ₹24,00,000. ₹8,00,000 premium ko chhod deta hai (wo bhi reserve hai, income nahi), ₹24,00,000 share capital ko other equity me gin leta hai, aur ₹5,00,000 sirf retained earnings leta hai.

questions.question: Ek company: current assets ₹18,00,000; trade payables ₹6,00,000; other current liabilities ₹2,00,000; term loan ₹12,00,000, jisme se ₹3,00,000 agle 12 mahine me due hai. Working capital kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Current liabilities = 6,00,000 + 2,00,000 + 3,00,000 (loan ki current maturity) = 11,00,000. Working capital = 18,00,000 − 11,00,000 = ₹7,00,000. ₹10,00,000 current maturity ko non-current me chhod deta hai, −₹2,00,000 poore loan ko current maan leta hai, aur ₹12,00,000 sirf trade payables ghatata hai.

questions.question: Ek company ke balance sheet items: PPE ₹30,00,000; capital work-in-progress ₹4,00,000; non-current investments ₹6,00,000; inventories ₹9,00,000; trade receivables ₹7,00,000; cash ₹3,00,000; equity share capital ₹15,00,000; other equity ?; long-term borrowings ₹10,00,000; trade payables ₹6,00,000; short-term borrowings ₹4,00,000; other current liabilities ₹2,00,000. Other equity aur working capital kitne hain?
questions.explanation: Non-current assets = 30 + 4 + 6 = 40 lakh; current assets = 9 + 7 + 3 = 19 lakh; total = 59,00,000. Liabilities = 10,00,000 + (6 + 4 + 2 = 12 lakh) = 22,00,000. Equity = 37,00,000 ⇒ other equity = 37,00,000 − 15,00,000 = ₹22,00,000. WC = 19,00,000 − 12,00,000 = ₹7,00,000. ₹37,00,000 total equity hai; WC ₹11,00,000 short-term borrowings ko current liabilities se bahar kar deta hai; ₹18,00,000 CWIP ko assets me ginna bhool jaata hai.

questions.question: Ek company ke 2,00,000 equity shares (face value ₹10) hain aur other equity ₹30,00,000 hai. Ab wo 50,000 naye shares ₹70 per share par issue karti hai aur poora paisa mil jaata hai. Issue ke baad book value per share kitni hogi?
questions.explanation: Pehle equity = 20,00,000 + 30,00,000 = 50,00,000. Naya paisa = 50,000 × 70 = 35,00,000 (5,00,000 share capital + 30,00,000 securities premium). Nayi equity = 85,00,000; shares = 2,50,000 ⇒ BVPS = ₹34.00. ₹25.00 issue se pehle ki value hai, ₹22.00 sirf face value jodta hai (premium bhi equity hai), aur ₹42.50 nayi equity ko purane shares se divide karta hai.

questions.question: 31 March ko ek company ke items: trade payables ₹8,00,000; 5 saal ka term loan ₹20,00,000 (jiski ₹4,00,000 ki instalment agle 12 mahine me due hai); customer advances ₹1,50,000; statutory dues (GST, TDS) ₹50,000; current tax liability ₹1,00,000; debentures ₹10,00,000 jo 3 saal baad due hain. Total current liabilities kitni hain?
questions.explanation: Current = trade payables 8,00,000 + loan ki current maturity 4,00,000 + customer advances 1,50,000 + statutory dues 50,000 + current tax 1,00,000 = ₹15,00,000. Debentures aur loan ka baaki 16,00,000 non-current hain. ₹11,00,000 current maturity bhool jaata hai, ₹31,00,000 poora loan current me daal deta hai, aur ₹13,50,000 customer advances ko liability nahi maanta.

questions.question: Ek company ka working capital ₹5,00,000 hai. Year-end se pehle: (i) ₹2,00,000 ka 5 saal ka loan liya aur cash bank me rakha; (ii) ₹1,00,000 cash se trade payables chukaye; (iii) ₹1,50,000 cash dekar machine khareedi. Ab working capital kitna hai?
questions.explanation: (i) Cash (current asset) +2,00,000, loan non-current ⇒ WC +2,00,000. (ii) Cash −1,00,000 aur payables −1,00,000 ⇒ WC same. (iii) Cash −1,50,000, machine non-current ⇒ WC −1,50,000. Naya WC = 5,00,000 + 2,00,000 − 1,50,000 = ₹5,50,000. ₹4,50,000 payables chukane ko bhi WC ghatana maanta hai, ₹7,00,000 machine wala cash bhool jaata hai, aur ₹3,50,000 long-term loan ko current liability bana deta hai.

weeks.title: Reading an annual report: the statement of profit and loss
weeks.summary: Is week aap Schedule III wala statement of profit and loss padhna seekhoge, aur revenue se gross profit, EBITDA, EBIT, PBT aur PAT tak ki seedhi chadh kar EPS nikaloge.
concepts: **Schedule III P&L ka structure**: Revenue from operations + Other income = Total income. Phir expenses: cost of materials consumed, purchases of stock-in-trade, **changes in inventories**, employee benefits expense, finance costs, depreciation and amortisation expense, other expenses. Total income − total expenses = profit before exceptional items and tax; phir exceptional items, tax expense (current + deferred), aur **profit for the year (PAT)**.

**Revenue from operations vs other income**: revenue from operations company ke main business se aata hai (sales, service fees). Other income side cheezon se — FD ka interest, dividend income, asset bechne par gain. Analysis me operating performance dekhne ke liye in dono ko alag rakho.

**Cost of goods sold aur gross profit**: trading company ke liye COGS = opening inventory + purchases − closing inventory. Schedule III me ye 'purchases' aur 'changes in inventories' (opening − closing) ke roop me dikhta hai. Gross profit = revenue − COGS; gross margin = GP ÷ revenue.

**EBITDA aur EBIT**: is course ka convention — EBITDA = revenue from operations − operating expenses (COGS, employee, other expenses), yaani depreciation, finance costs aur tax se pehle, aur other income ke bina. EBIT = EBITDA − depreciation and amortisation. Kai companies aur analysts other income bhi jod dete hain, isliye report me definition zaroor dekho.

**PBT aur PAT**: PBT = EBIT + other income − finance costs (exceptional items ho to unhe bhi). PAT = PBT − tax expense. Net profit margin = PAT ÷ revenue. Ek shortcut ulta bhi chalta hai: EBITDA = PAT + tax + finance costs + depreciation (jab other income aur exceptional items na hon).

**Other comprehensive income (OCI)**: kuch gains/losses (jaise employee benefit plans ke remeasurement) P&L ke neeche OCI me aate hain. PAT + OCI = total comprehensive income. EPS PAT par nikalta hai, total comprehensive income par nahi.

**Earnings per share (EPS)**: basic EPS = (PAT − preference dividend) ÷ weighted average number of equity shares. Saal ke beech me naye shares issue hue to unhe sirf utne hisse ke liye gino jitne time wo outstanding the. Diluted EPS me convertible instruments ka potential effect bhi jodte hain.

example.problem: Fictional company 'Ganga Appliances Ltd': revenue from operations ₹50,00,000; COGS ₹30,00,000; employee benefits ₹6,00,000; other expenses ₹4,00,000; depreciation ₹2,00,000; finance costs ₹1,00,000; other income nahi; tax rate 25%; 2,50,000 equity shares saal bhar outstanding. GP, EBITDA, EBIT, PBT, PAT aur EPS nikalo.

mistakes: Changes in inventories ka sign ulta lagana. Closing inventory opening se zyada hai to inventory badhi — COGS purchases se kam hoga, zyada nahi.
EPS me saal ke end ke shares lena jabki naye shares beech saal me aaye. Weighted average shares lo.
EBITDA me other income jodna ya na jodna bina bataye mix karna. Ek convention chuno aur wahi follow karo; companies ke beech compare karte waqt definition check karo.
revision: GP = revenue − COGS.
EBITDA − D&A = EBIT; EBIT + other income − finance costs = PBT.
PAT = PBT − tax; EBITDA = PAT + tax + finance + D&A (no other income).
Basic EPS = (PAT − preference dividend) ÷ weighted average shares.
Total comprehensive income = PAT + OCI.

questions.question: Ek company ka revenue ₹8,00,000 aur cost of goods sold ₹4,80,000 hai. Gross profit margin kya hai?
questions.explanation: GP = 8,00,000 − 4,80,000 = 3,20,000. Margin = 3,20,000 ÷ 8,00,000 = 40%. 66.7% tab aata hai jab GP ko COGS se divide karte ho (wo markup hai, margin nahi); 60% COGS ka revenue me share hai.

questions.question: EBITDA se EBIT tak pahunchne ke liye kya ghatana padta hai?
questions.explanation: EBIT = EBITDA − D&A; naam me hi 'DA' hat jaata hai. Finance costs EBIT ke baad (PBT tak pahunchne me) ghatte hain, aur tax PBT ke baad — dono EBIT ke neeche ki seedhi hain.

questions.question: Ek company ka PAT ₹6,00,000, tax expense ₹2,00,000, finance costs ₹1,50,000 aur depreciation ₹2,50,000 hai. Koi other income ya exceptional item nahi hai. EBITDA kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Neeche se upar jodo: PAT 6,00,000 + tax 2,00,000 = PBT 8,00,000; + finance 1,50,000 = EBIT 9,50,000; + depreciation 2,50,000 = EBITDA ₹12,00,000. ₹9,50,000 EBIT hai (depreciation jodna bhool gaye) aur ₹8,00,000 sirf PBT hai.

questions.question: Ek company: revenue from operations ₹60,00,000; other income (FD interest) ₹4,00,000; total expenses ₹50,00,000, jisme depreciation ₹3,00,000 aur finance costs ₹2,00,000 shaamil hain. Agar EBITDA me other income nahi jodte, to EBITDA kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Operating expenses (D&A aur finance ke bina) = 50,00,000 − 3,00,000 − 2,00,000 = 45,00,000. EBITDA = 60,00,000 − 45,00,000 = ₹15,00,000. ₹19,00,000 other income jodne se aata hai (jo is question ka convention nahi), aur ₹14,00,000 PBT hai (64,00,000 − 50,00,000).

questions.question: Ek trading company: revenue ₹10,00,000; purchases of stock-in-trade ₹7,00,000; opening inventory ₹1,50,000; closing inventory ₹2,00,000. Gross profit kitna hai?
questions.explanation: COGS = 1,50,000 + 7,00,000 − 2,00,000 = 6,50,000 (change in inventories = opening − closing = −50,000). GP = 10,00,000 − 6,50,000 = ₹3,50,000. ₹3,00,000 inventory change ignore karne se, aur ₹2,50,000 change ka sign ulta (+50,000) lagane se aata hai.
