questions.question: Ek company ka PAT ₹45,00,000 hai aur preference dividend ₹5,00,000. 1 April ko 8,00,000 equity shares the; 1 October ko 4,00,000 naye shares issue hue (financial year 1 April – 31 March). Basic EPS kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Naye shares saal ke 6 mahine outstanding the: weighted shares = 8,00,000 + 4,00,000 × 6/12 = 10,00,000. Equity ka profit = 45,00,000 − 5,00,000 = 40,00,000. EPS = ₹4.00. ₹3.33 year-end ke 12,00,000 shares lene se, ₹4.50 preference dividend na ghatane se, ₹5.00 sirf opening shares lene se aata hai.

questions.question: Ek textile company ko fixed deposits par ₹2,00,000 interest mila. Schedule III statement of profit and loss me ye kahan dikhega?
questions.explanation: Textile company ka main business kapda bechna hai; FD interest side income hai, isliye other income. Revenue from operations sirf main business (sales, service fees) ke liye hai. Finance costs wo interest hai jo company deti hai, jo usse milta hai wo nahi.

questions.question: Ek company ka revenue from operations ₹40,00,000 aur PAT ₹3,00,000 hai. Net profit margin kya hai?
questions.explanation: Net profit margin = PAT ÷ revenue = 3,00,000 ÷ 40,00,000 = 7.5%. 13.33% ulta divide karne (revenue ÷ PAT) se aata hai, aur 75% / 0.75% decimal galat lagane se.

questions.question: Ek company ka PAT ₹12,00,000 hai (tax already ghat chuka), koi preference shares nahi, aur poore saal 4,00,000 equity shares outstanding rahe. Basic EPS kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Basic EPS = PAT ÷ shares = 12,00,000 ÷ 4,00,000 = ₹3.00. ₹0.33 ulta divide karta hai, ₹2.25 PAT par dobara 25% tax laga deta hai (PAT me tax pehle hi ghat chuka), aur ₹30.00 decimal ki galti hai.

questions.question: Ek company ka PBT ₹14,00,000 hai. Finance costs ₹3,00,000, other income ₹1,00,000 aur depreciation ₹2,00,000 hain. Koi exceptional item nahi. Course ke convention (EBIT me other income nahi) se EBIT kitna hai?
questions.explanation: PBT = EBIT + other income − finance costs ⇒ EBIT = 14,00,000 − 1,00,000 + 3,00,000 = ₹16,00,000. ₹17,00,000 other income ko hatana bhool jaata hai, ₹18,00,000 EBITDA hai (depreciation bhi jod diya), aur ₹11,00,000 finance costs ko jodne ki jagah ghata deta hai.

questions.question: Ek company ka PAT ₹20,00,000 hai. Employee benefit plan ke remeasurement se OCI me ₹1,50,000 ka loss aaya. Poore saal 10,00,000 equity shares outstanding rahe, koi preference share nahi. Total comprehensive income aur basic EPS kya hain?
questions.explanation: TCI = PAT + OCI = 20,00,000 − 1,50,000 = ₹18,50,000. EPS PAT par nikalta hai: 20,00,000 ÷ 10,00,000 = ₹2.00. ₹1.85 EPS ko TCI par nikalta hai, ₹21,50,000 OCI loss ko gain maan leta hai, aur ₹20,00,000 OCI ko bilkul chhod deta hai.

questions.question: Ek trading company: revenue from operations ₹80,00,000; other income ₹2,00,000; purchases of stock-in-trade ₹50,00,000; opening inventory ₹6,00,000; closing inventory ₹10,00,000; employee benefits ₹8,00,000; other expenses ₹5,00,000; depreciation ₹3,00,000; finance costs ₹2,00,000; tax rate 25%. PAT kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Changes in inventories = 6,00,000 − 10,00,000 = −4,00,000 ⇒ COGS = 46,00,000. EBITDA = 80 − 46 − 8 − 5 = 21 lakh; EBIT = 18 lakh; PBT = 18 + 2 (other income) − 2 (finance costs) = 18,00,000. Tax 4,50,000 ⇒ PAT ₹13,50,000. ₹7,50,000 inventory change ka sign ulta karta hai (COGS 54 lakh), ₹12,00,000 other income bhool jaata hai, aur ₹18,00,000 PBT hai, tax ghatana baaki.

questions.question: Ek company ka PAT ₹62,00,000 aur preference dividend ₹2,00,000 hai. 1 April ko 10,00,000 equity shares the; 1 January ko 4,00,000 naye shares issue hue (financial year 1 April – 31 March). Basic EPS kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Equity holders ka profit = 62,00,000 − 2,00,000 = 60,00,000. Naye shares sirf Jan–Mar = 3 mahine outstanding: weighted shares = 10,00,000 + 4,00,000 × 3/12 = 11,00,000. EPS = 60,00,000 ÷ 11,00,000 = ₹5.45. ₹4.29 year-end ke 14,00,000 shares leta hai, ₹5.64 preference dividend nahi ghatata, aur ₹6.00 naye shares ko bilkul ignore karta hai.

questions.question: Ek company ka revenue from operations ₹60,00,000 aur net profit margin 10% hai. Tax PBT ka 25% hai. Finance costs ₹1,00,000 aur depreciation ₹3,00,000 hain; koi other income ya exceptional item nahi. EBITDA margin kya hai?
questions.explanation: PAT = 60,00,000 × 10% = 6,00,000. PBT = 6,00,000 ÷ 75% = 8,00,000. EBITDA = PBT + finance costs + depreciation = 8,00,000 + 1,00,000 + 3,00,000 = 12,00,000 ⇒ margin 20%. 16.67% tax wapas jodna bhool jaata hai (PAT se shuru), 19.17% tax ko PAT ka 25% maan leta hai, aur 15% EBIT margin hai (depreciation nahi joda).

questions.question: Ek company ka profit before exceptional items and tax ₹30,00,000 hai. Factory me aag lagne se ₹6,00,000 ka exceptional loss hua. Tax PBT ka 25% hai. OCI me ₹2,00,000 ka gain aaya. Poore saal 6,00,000 equity shares rahe, koi preference share nahi. Basic EPS kitna hai?
questions.explanation: PBT = 30,00,000 − 6,00,000 = 24,00,000. Tax = 6,00,000 ⇒ PAT = 18,00,000. EPS = 18,00,000 ÷ 6,00,000 = ₹3.00 (OCI EPS me nahi aata). ₹3.75 exceptional loss ignore karta hai, ₹3.33 OCI gain ko PAT me jod deta hai, aur ₹2.75 tax exceptional item se pehle wale ₹30,00,000 par laga deta hai.

weeks.title: Journal, ledger and trial balance
weeks.summary: Is week aap debit aur credit ke rules pakke karoge, transactions ko journal me likhna aur ledger me post karna seekhoge, aur trial balance banake samjhoge ki wo kaunsi galtiyan pakadta hai aur kaunsi nahi.
concepts: **Accounting cycle**: source document (invoice, receipt, bank statement) → **journal** me entry → **ledger** me posting → **trial balance** → year-end adjustments → financial statements. Aaj ye sab accounting software karta hai, par logic wahi hai — software bhi andar se double entry hi chalata hai.

**Debit-credit rules (equation wala tareeka)**: jo accounts equation ke left side wale hain unka increase debit — assets, expenses, aur drawings/dividends. Right side wale accounts ka increase credit — liabilities, equity (capital), aur revenue/income. Decrease ke liye ulta. Har entry me total debit = total credit.

**Traditional golden rules** (Indian textbooks me common): personal account — debit the receiver, credit the giver; real account (assets) — debit what comes in, credit what goes out; nominal account (expenses, incomes) — debit all expenses and losses, credit all incomes and gains. Dono tareekon se same entry aati hai; jo samajh aaye wo use karo.

**Journal**: transactions ka chronological record — date, debit account (Dr), credit account (Cr), amount aur **narration** (chhoti explanation). Ek se zyada debit ya credit ho to **compound entry**. Jaise maal ₹30,000 ka khareeda, ₹10,000 cash diya aur ₹20,000 udhaar: Dr Purchases 30,000; Cr Cash 10,000; Cr Supplier 20,000.

**Ledger**: har account ka alag page (T-account) — left me debits, right me credits. Journal se har amount apne account me **post** hota hai. Period end par account **balance** karte hain: zyada wale side ka total minus kam wala = balance, jo 'balance c/d' likh kar agle period me 'balance b/d' banta hai.
**Normal balances**: assets, expenses aur drawings ka balance aam taur par debit; liabilities, capital aur revenue ka credit. Cash ka credit balance (bank overdraft ke alawa) matlab kahin galti hai.

**Trial balance**: saare ledger balances ki list, debit aur credit column me. Dono totals barabar hon to arithmetic sahi lagta hai — par sab sahi hai ye guarantee nahi. **Errors jo TB pakadta hai**: ek hi side post hona, galat totalling, debit aur credit me alag amount. **Errors jo nahi pakadta**: entry poori chhoot jaana (omission), galat party ke account me (commission), capital vs revenue ki galti (principle), do galtiyan jo ek doosre ko cancel karein (compensating), original entry me hi galat amount, ya poori entry ulti (reversal). Farq ho to temporarily **suspense account** use karte hain.

example.problem: Fictional dukaan 'Gupta Electricals' ke transactions: (1) ₹1,00,000 cash se business shuru; (2) ₹25,000 cash me furniture; (3) Mehta Traders (fictional) se ₹40,000 ka maal credit par; (4) ₹30,000 ka maal cash me becha; (5) ₹5,000 rent cash me diya. Journal entries, cash ka balance aur trial balance banao.
steps: (1) Cash (asset ↑) debit, Capital (equity ↑) credit. (2) Furniture debit, Cash credit.
(4) Cash debit, Sales (revenue ↑) credit. (5) Rent (expense ↑) debit, Cash credit.
Trial balance debit side: Cash 1,00,000 + Furniture 25,000 + Purchases 40,000 + Rent 5,000 = 1,70,000.
Credit side: Capital 1,00,000 + Mehta Traders 40,000 + Sales 30,000 = 1,70,000. Answer: **trial balance ₹1,70,000 par agree karta hai**.
example.code:
Journal (Gupta Electricals)
(1) Cash A/c            Dr  1,00,000
        To Capital A/c            1,00,000
(2) Furniture A/c       Dr    25,000
        To Cash A/c                 25,000
(3) Purchases A/c       Dr    40,000
        To Mehta Traders A/c        40,000
(4) Cash A/c            Dr    30,000
        To Sales A/c                30,000
(5) Rent A/c            Dr     5,000
        To Cash A/c                  5,000

mistakes: Customer se paisa aane par Sales ko credit kar dena. Sale pehle hi record ho chuki thi; ab receivable (customer ka account) credit hoga, warna revenue double ho jaayega.
Trial balance agree hone ko 'books bilkul sahi hain' samajhna. Omission, commission, principle aur compensating errors ke baad bhi totals barabar rehte hain.
Drawings ko credit balance samajhna kyunki wo equity se juda hai. Drawings equity ko ghatate hain, isliye unka normal balance debit hai.
revision: Debit ↑: assets, expenses, drawings. Credit ↑: liabilities, equity, revenue.
Journal = date-wise; ledger = account-wise.
Trial balance: total Dr = total Cr, sirf arithmetic check.
TB nahi pakadta: omission, commission, principle, compensating, original entry, reversal.
Farq ho to suspense account, galti milne par use clear karo.

questions.question: Business ne staff ko ₹15,000 salary cash me di. Sahi journal entry kya hai?
questions.explanation: Salary expense badha ⇒ debit; cash (asset) ghata ⇒ credit. Pehla option ulta hai. Capital tab debit hota jab owner khud ke liye paisa nikaalta (drawings) — staff ki salary business ka expense hai.

questions.question: Inme se kis account ka normal balance **debit** hota hai?
questions.explanation: Drawings owner ki equity ko ghatate hain, isliye unka increase debit hota hai aur normal balance debit. Trade payables (liability), share capital (equity) aur revenue — teeno badhne par credit hote hain. Drawings ko equity jaisa credit samajhna common trap hai.

questions.question: Ramesh ko pichhle mahine credit par maal becha tha. Aaj Ramesh ne ₹20,000 cash me chuka diye. Sahi entry kya hai?
questions.explanation: Cash (asset) badha ⇒ debit; Ramesh par baaki receivable (asset) ghata ⇒ credit. Sales ko credit karna sabse bada trap hai — sale pichhle mahine hi record ho chuki thi, dobara karoge to revenue double ho jaayega.

questions.question: Cash account ka opening balance ₹12,000 debit hai. Mahine me receipts ₹45,000 aur ₹8,000; payments ₹20,000, ₹30,000 aur ₹4,500. Mahine ke end me cash account ka balance kya hai?
questions.explanation: Debit side = 12,000 + 45,000 + 8,000 = 65,000; credit side = 20,000 + 30,000 + 4,500 = 54,500. Balance = ₹10,500 debit (debit side bada hai). ₹1,500 credit opening balance bhoolne se aata hai, aur ₹15,000 ek payment (4,500) chhodne se.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsi galti trial balance ke totals me farq **nahi** laati?
options: Ek entry ka sirf debit side post hua
Ek ledger account ka total galat joda gaya
Debit me ₹500 aur credit me ₹5,000 post hua
Nayi machinery ki purchase Repairs account me debit ho gayi
questions.explanation: Machinery ko Repairs me debit karna error of principle hai: debit aur credit dono barabar hain, bas galat type ke account me — TB agree karega, par profit kam aur assets kam dikhenge. Baaki teeno galtiyan ek side ko doosre se alag kar deti hain, isliye TB me farq aata hai.

questions.question: Ek trial balance me debit total ₹2,45,000 aur credit total ₹2,52,000 hai. Do galtiyan mili: (a) ₹3,500 rent cash account me sahi credit hua par Rent account me post hi nahi hua; (b) ₹1,750 ka sales return, Sales Returns account ke debit ki jagah credit side me post ho gaya. Dono theek karne ke baad trial balance ka total kya hoga?
questions.explanation: (a) Rent ka debit jodo: debit 2,45,000 + 3,500 = 2,48,500. (b) Sales returns ko credit se hatao aur debit me daalo: debit 2,48,500 + 1,750 = 2,50,250; credit 2,52,000 − 1,750 = 2,50,250. Dono barabar. ₹2,48,500 sirf pehli galti theek karne se aata hai; ₹2,53,750 tab jab return ko credit se hatane ki jagah aur jod dete ho.

questions.question: Business ne 'Sharma Furnishers' se ₹18,000 ka office furniture credit par khareeda. Sahi journal entry kya hai?
questions.explanation: Furniture ek asset aaya (debit), aur Sharma Furnishers ko paisa dena hai — liability badhi (credit). Purchases account sirf bechne wale maal ke liye hai, furniture ke liye nahi. Cash credit galat hai kyunki payment abhi hua hi nahi.

questions.question: Traditional golden rules me **real account** (assets) ke liye rule kya hai?
options: Debit the receiver, credit the giver
Debit what comes in, credit what goes out
Debit all expenses and losses, credit all incomes and gains
Debit what goes out, credit what comes in
questions.explanation: Real accounts (assets) ke liye: jo cheez business me aaye use debit, jo bahar jaaye use credit. 'Debit the receiver, credit the giver' personal accounts ka rule hai, aur expenses/incomes wala rule nominal accounts ka. Aakhri option real account rule ko ulta kar deta hai.

questions.question: Inme se kis account ka normal balance **credit** hota hai?
questions.explanation: Outstanding salary ek liability hai, aur liabilities ka normal balance credit hota hai. Rent (expense), cash (asset) aur drawings — teeno ka normal balance debit. Drawings equity se jude hain, isliye unhe credit samajhna common trap hai.

questions.question: Business ne ₹50,000 ka maal 'Verma Stores' ko becha: ₹15,000 turant cash me mile aur baaki Verma Stores baad me dega. Sahi compound journal entry kya hai?
options: Dr Cash ₹15,000; Dr Verma Stores ₹35,000; Cr Sales ₹50,000
Dr Sales ₹50,000; Cr Cash ₹15,000; Cr Verma Stores ₹35,000
Dr Cash ₹15,000; Dr Verma Stores ₹35,000; Cr Purchases ₹50,000
questions.explanation: Cash (asset) 15,000 aaya aur Verma Stores par 35,000 baaki (receivable, asset) — dono debit. Sale ka poora 50,000 revenue credit. Doosra option poori entry ulti kar deta hai, teesra poore amount ko cash maan leta hai, aur chautha sales ki jagah Purchases credit karta hai.

questions.question: Mohan ko ₹8,000 ka maal credit par becha gaya, par posting me galti se Sohan ke account me debit ho gaya (Sales sahi credit hua). Ye kaunsa error hai, aur kya trial balance agree karega?
options: Error of principle; trial balance agree nahi karega
Error of omission; trial balance agree karega
Error of commission; trial balance agree karega
Error of commission; trial balance agree nahi karega
questions.explanation: Amount sahi side (debit) me post hua, bas galat party ke account me — ye error of commission hai. Debit aur credit dono 8,000 hain, isliye totals barabar rehte hain aur TB ise nahi pakadta. Principle capital vs revenue ki galti hoti hai, aur omission me entry poori chhoot jaati hai.

questions.question: Ek dukaan ke ledger balances: Cash ₹42,000; Furniture ₹60,000; Purchases ₹1,30,000; Sales ₹2,10,000; Rent ₹24,000; Trade payables ₹36,000; Trade receivables ₹55,000; Drawings ₹15,000; Salary ₹40,000; Bank loan ₹50,000; Capital ?. Trial balance agree karne ke liye Capital kitna hoga, aur TB ka total kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Debit balances: Cash 42,000 + Furniture 60,000 + Purchases 1,30,000 + Rent 24,000 + Receivables 55,000 + Drawings 15,000 + Salary 40,000 = 3,66,000. Credit: Sales 2,10,000 + Payables 36,000 + Loan 50,000 = 2,96,000 ⇒ Capital = ₹70,000, total ₹3,66,000. ₹40,000 drawings ko credit side me daalta hai, ₹1,70,000 bank loan ko debit, aur ₹22,000 rent ko credit.

questions.question: Supplier 'Kapoor Traders' ke account ka opening balance ₹25,000 credit hai (humein dena hai). Mahine me: ₹60,000 ka maal unse credit par khareeda; unhe ₹40,000 cash diye; ₹5,000 ka kharab maal unhe wapas kiya (purchase return). Mahine ke end me Kapoor Traders ke account ka balance kya hai?
questions.explanation: Credit side: opening 25,000 + purchase 60,000 = 85,000. Debit side: payment 40,000 + return 5,000 = 45,000. Balance = ₹40,000 credit (abhi bhi itna dena hai). ₹40,000 debit side ulta karta hai, ₹50,000 return ko liability badhana maan leta hai, aur ₹10,000 opening ko debit balance maan kar chalta hai.

questions.question: Ek trial balance me debit total ₹4,80,000 aur credit total ₹4,92,500 hai. Teen galtiyan mili: (a) ₹6,000 ki salary Salary account me sirf ₹600 post hui (cash sahi credit hua); (b) ₹7,100 ki credit sale customer ke account me post hi nahi hui (Sales sahi credit hua); (c) ₹2,000 ki furniture purchase Purchases account me debit ho gayi. Teeno theek karne ke baad trial balance ka total kya hoga?
questions.explanation: (a) Salary debit 5,400 kam tha ⇒ debit +5,400. (b) Customer ka debit 7,100 missing ⇒ debit +7,100. (c) Error of principle: Purchases se Furniture me shift, dono debit — total par asar nahi. Debit = 4,80,000 + 5,400 + 7,100 = 4,92,500 = credit. ₹4,93,100 poore 6,000 jodta hai, ₹4,94,500 (c) ko bhi total me jod deta hai, aur ₹4,85,400 sirf (a) theek karta hai.

questions.question: Ek naye business ke mahine ke transactions: (1) ₹3,00,000 capital bank me jama; (2) 'Anand Traders' se ₹1,20,000 ka maal credit par; (3) 'Neha Retail' ko ₹1,40,000 ka maal credit par becha; (4) Neha se ₹1,00,000 bank me mile; (5) Anand ko ₹70,000 bank se diye; (6) ₹12,000 bijli bill bank se bhara. Accounts balance karke trial balance ka total kya aayega?
questions.explanation: Bank = 3,00,000 + 1,00,000 − 70,000 − 12,000 = 3,18,000 Dr. Debit: Bank 3,18,000 + Purchases 1,20,000 + Neha 40,000 + Electricity 12,000 = 4,90,000. Credit: Capital 3,00,000 + Anand 50,000 + Sales 1,40,000 = 4,90,000. ₹5,90,000 Neha ki receipt ko Sales me credit kar deta hai (revenue double); ₹5,60,000 Anand ka account balance nahi karta (gross 1,20,000 aur 70,000 alag likhta hai); ₹6,60,000 Neha aur Anand dono ko balance nahi karta.

weeks.title: Cash flow statement: operating activities
weeks.summary: Is week aap samjhoge ki profit aur cash alag kyun hote hain, aur indirect method se cash flow from operating activities banaoge — non-cash items wapas jodna, working capital changes adjust karna, aur tax paid ghatana.
concepts: **Profit ≠ cash**: P&L accrual basis par banta hai — credit sales, depreciation, outstanding expenses sab profit ko badalte hain bina cash hile. Cash flow statement (Ind AS 7) batata hai ki saal me **cash and cash equivalents** (cash, bank balance, aur 3 mahine tak ke highly liquid investments) asal me kahan se aaye aur kahan gaye. Profitable company bhi cash ki kami se doob sakti hai.

**Teen activities**: operating (main business se — customers se receipts, suppliers aur staff ko payments, tax), investing (long-term assets aur investments khareedna/bechna), financing (owners aur lenders ke saath — shares, loans, dividends, interest). Is week sirf operating; baaki do agle week.

**Direct vs indirect method**: direct method seedha cash receipts aur payments dikhata hai. **Indirect method** profit se shuru karke adjust karta hai — Indian listed companies aksar yahi use karti hain, aur profit before tax (PBT) se shuru karti hain. Is course me bhi indirect method, PBT se (ya jahan tax na ho wahan net profit se).

**Non-cash aur non-operating adjustments**: depreciation, amortisation, impairment jaise non-cash expenses wapas **jodo**. Asset bechne par loss jodo aur gain **ghatao** — kyunki poori sale proceeds investing me dikhegi. Is course ka convention (Ind AS 7 bhi non-financial companies ke liye yahi kehta hai): finance costs wapas jodo (interest paid financing me jaayega) aur interest/dividend income ghatao (received amount investing me jaayega).

**Working capital changes**: current operating asset (receivables, inventory, prepaid) badha ⇒ cash phansa ⇒ **ghatao**; ghata ⇒ jodo. Current operating liability (trade payables, outstanding expenses, customer advances) badhi ⇒ cash bacha ⇒ **jodo**; ghati ⇒ ghatao. Yaad rakhne ka tareeka: asset ka badlav ulta sign, liability ka badlav seedha sign.

**Income tax paid**: P&L ka tax expense nahi, asal me bhara gaya tax ghatate hain. Tax paid = opening tax payable + tax expense − closing tax payable. Isiliye PBT se shuru karna saaf rehta hai — tax ek hi baar, cash ke roop me, ghatta hai.

**Format**: PBT → (+) non-cash/non-operating adjustments = operating profit before working capital changes → (±) working capital changes = cash generated from operations → (−) income tax paid = **net cash from operating activities (CFO)**.

example.problem: Fictional company 'Asha Packaging Ltd': PBT ₹5,00,000; depreciation ₹80,000; machine bechne par loss ₹10,000; finance costs ₹30,000; trade receivables ₹60,000 badhe; inventory ₹25,000 ghati; trade payables ₹15,000 badhe; outstanding expenses ₹5,000 ghate; income tax paid ₹1,20,000. CFO nikalo.
steps: Payables badhe ⇒ +15,000; outstanding expenses ghate ⇒ −5,000. Net working capital effect = −25,000.
example.code:
Profit before tax                         5,00,000
  + Depreciation                            80,000
  + Loss on sale of machine                 10,000
  + Finance costs                           30,000
Operating profit before WC changes        6,20,000
  - Increase in trade receivables          (60,000)
  + Decrease in inventories                 25,000
  + Increase in trade payables              15,000
  - Decrease in outstanding expenses        (5,000)
Cash generated from operations            5,95,000
  - Income tax paid                       (1,20,000)
Net cash from operating activities        4,75,000

mistakes: Working capital ke sign ulte lagana. Receivables ya inventory badhe to cash kam hua (ghatao); payables badhe to cash bacha (jodo).
Asset bechne ka gain CFO me rehne dena. Gain profit me already hai, use ghatao, kyunki poora sale amount investing activities me aayega — warna wo double count hoga.
Tax expense ko tax paid samajhna. Tax payable ke opening aur closing balance se asli cash tax nikalo.
revision: CFO (indirect) = PBT + non-cash items ± WC changes − tax paid.
Depreciation, loss on sale: jodo. Gain on sale, interest income: ghatao.
Current asset ↑ ⇒ ghatao; current liability ↑ ⇒ jodo.
Tax paid = opening payable + expense − closing payable.
Finance costs wapas jodo; interest paid financing me dikhega.

questions.question: Indirect method me depreciation ko profit me wapas kyun jodte hain?
options: Ye non-cash expense hai — isne profit ghataya par is saal cash bahar nahi gaya
Depreciation se company ko cash milta hai
questions.explanation: Machine ka cash to khareedte waqt (investing me) ja chuka; depreciation sirf us cost ko saalon me baantna hai. Profit se ghata tha par cash nahi hila, isliye wapas jodte hain. Ye cash ka source nahi hai — ye sabse common galatfahmi hai.

questions.question: Saal me trade receivables ₹2,00,000 se badh kar ₹2,80,000 ho gaye. Indirect method me CFO nikalte waqt iske saath kya karenge?
options: Ignore karenge, ye balance sheet item hai
questions.explanation: Receivables badhne ka matlab: kuch sales profit me hain par unka cash abhi nahi aaya. Isliye badhotri ₹80,000 ghatao. Jodna tab hota jab receivables ghatte (purane udhaar wasool hote).

questions.question: Ek proprietorship (tax ignore karo) ka net profit ₹2,00,000 hai. Depreciation ₹40,000; inventory ₹30,000 badhi; trade payables ₹20,000 badhe; trade receivables ₹25,000 badhe. Cash from operating activities kitna hai?
questions.explanation: 2,00,000 + 40,000 − 30,000 (inventory ↑) + 20,000 (payables ↑) − 25,000 (receivables ↑) = ₹2,05,000. ₹2,75,000 working capital ke sign ulte lagane se aata hai, ₹1,25,000 depreciation ghatane se, aur ₹2,40,000 working capital ignore karne se.

questions.question: Ek company ne purana equipment ₹65,000 me becha; carrying amount ₹50,000 tha, isliye P&L me ₹15,000 gain aaya. Cash flow statement me sahi treatment kya hai?
options: CFO me ₹15,000 jodo, kyunki cash aaya
Gain ko ignore karo, kuch adjust mat karo
CFO me ₹15,000 ghatao; poore ₹65,000 investing activities me inflow dikhao
questions.explanation: Equipment bechna investing activity hai, isliye poora cash ₹65,000 investing me. Gain ₹15,000 profit me pehle se hai — use CFO se ghatao, warna wo do baar gina jaayega. Gain ko ignore karna isi double counting ka trap hai.

questions.question: Ek company ka is saal ka tax expense ₹1,50,000 hai. Tax payable ka opening balance ₹40,000 aur closing balance ₹55,000 hai. Saal me kitna income tax cash me bhara gaya?
questions.explanation: Tax paid = opening 40,000 + expense 1,50,000 − closing 55,000 = ₹1,35,000. Payable badha, matlab poora expense abhi nahi bhara. ₹1,65,000 opening aur closing ko ulta lagane se aata hai; ₹1,50,000 expense ko hi paid maanne se.

questions.question: Ek company: PBT ₹8,00,000; depreciation ₹1,20,000; finance costs ₹50,000; interest income ₹20,000; trade receivables ₹70,000 badhe; inventory ₹30,000 ghati; trade payables ₹40,000 ghate; income tax paid ₹1,80,000. Course ke convention (interest paid financing me, interest received investing me) se CFO kitna hai?
questions.explanation: 8,00,000 + 1,20,000 + 50,000 − 20,000 = 9,50,000. WC: −70,000 + 30,000 − 40,000 = −80,000 ⇒ 8,70,000. Tax: − 1,80,000 ⇒ ₹6,90,000. ₹8,70,000 tax bhoolne se, ₹7,70,000 payables ki kami ko jodne se (ghatana tha), aur ₹6,60,000 finance cost aur interest income adjust na karne se aata hai.

questions.question: Ek manufacturing company ke in cash flows me se kaunsa **operating activity** hai?
options: Suppliers ko raw material ke liye payment
Bank se naya term loan lena
questions.explanation: Suppliers ko payment main business chalane ka hissa hai, isliye operating. Machine khareedna investing hai (long-term asset), aur loan lena ya dividend dena financing (owners aur lenders ke saath). Dividend ko 'regular kharch' maan kar operating me daalna common galti hai.

questions.question: Saal me ek company ki inventory ₹1,50,000 se ghat kar ₹1,10,000 reh gayi. Indirect method me CFO nikalte waqt iske saath kya karenge?
options: Ignore karenge, ye balance sheet item hai
questions.explanation: Inventory (current operating asset) ghati, matlab purana maal bika aur cash usme phansa nahi — isliye ₹40,000 jodo. Asset ka badlav ulta sign leta hai: badhe to ghatao, ghate to jodo. Sirf badlav adjust hota hai, closing balance (₹1,10,000) nahi.

questions.question: Ind AS 7 ke hisaab se 'cash and cash equivalents' me kya shaamil hai?
options: Cash, bank balance aur saari trade receivables
Cash, bank balance aur 3 mahine tak ke highly liquid investments
Cash, bank balance aur 5 saal ke fixed deposits
questions.explanation: Cash and cash equivalents = cash, bank balance, aur aise highly liquid investments jo 3 mahine ke andar cash ban jaayein. Receivables abhi cash nahi hain (customer ne paisa diya nahi), aur 5 saal ki FD lambi investment hai, cash equivalent nahi. Sirf haath ka cash lena definition ko bahut chhota kar deta hai.

questions.question: Ek proprietorship (tax ignore karo) ka net profit ₹3,50,000 hai. Depreciation ₹60,000; furniture bechne par loss ₹8,000; prepaid expenses ₹5,000 badhe; outstanding expenses ₹12,000 badhe; trade receivables ₹30,000 ghate. Cash from operating activities kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Adjustments: 3,50,000 + 60,000 + 8,000 (loss wapas jodo) = 4,18,000. WC: prepaid badhe −5,000; outstanding badhe +12,000; receivables ghate +30,000 ⇒ +37,000. CFO = ₹4,55,000. ₹4,39,000 loss ko ghata deta hai (gain jaisa), ₹3,81,000 WC ke saare sign ulte karta hai, aur ₹3,95,000 depreciation wapas jodna bhool jaata hai.

questions.question: Ek company ka is saal ka tax expense ₹2,40,000 hai. Tax payable ka opening balance ₹65,000 aur closing balance ₹30,000 hai. Saal me kitna income tax cash me bhara gaya?
questions.explanation: Tax paid = opening payable + tax expense − closing payable = 65,000 + 2,40,000 − 30,000 = ₹2,75,000. Payable ghata, matlab company ne expense se zyada bhara. ₹2,05,000 opening aur closing ko ulta laga deta hai, ₹2,40,000 expense ko hi paid maan leta hai, aur ₹35,000 sirf payable ka badlav hai.

questions.question: Ek company: PBT ₹12,00,000; depreciation ₹2,00,000; investment bechne par gain ₹50,000; dividend income ₹30,000; finance costs ₹80,000; trade receivables ₹1,00,000 badhe; inventory ₹60,000 badhi; trade payables ₹90,000 badhe; customer advances ₹20,000 ghate. Tax expense ₹3,00,000; tax payable opening ₹40,000, closing ₹60,000. Course convention se CFO kitna hai?

Direct method se CFO nikalo. Saari sales credit par: revenue ₹20,00,000; trade receivables opening ₹3,00,000, closing ₹3,80,000. Saari purchases credit par: purchases ₹12,00,000; trade payables opening ₹1,50,000, closing ₹2,10,000. Operating expenses ₹3,00,000 cash me diye, aur income tax ₹1,00,000 bhara. Net cash from operating activities kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Customers se cash = 20,00,000 + 3,00,000 − 3,80,000 = 19,20,000. Suppliers ko cash = 12,00,000 + 1,50,000 − 2,10,000 = 11,40,000. CFO = 19,20,000 − 11,40,000 − 3,00,000 − 1,00,000 = ₹3,80,000. ₹5,40,000 receivables ka badlav ulta lagata hai, ₹2,60,000 payables ka, aur ₹4,00,000 revenue aur purchases ko hi cash maan leta hai.

questions.question: Ek company ka net cash from operating activities ₹7,50,000 hai. Indirect method ke items: depreciation ₹1,50,000; finance costs ₹60,000; interest income ₹40,000; inventory ₹80,000 badhi; trade payables ₹50,000 badhe; income tax paid ₹2,00,000. Course convention se company ka PBT kitna tha?
questions.explanation: CFO = PBT + 1,50,000 + 60,000 − 40,000 − 80,000 + 50,000 − 2,00,000 = PBT − 60,000. To PBT = 7,50,000 + 60,000 = ₹8,10,000. ₹6,90,000 net adjustment ko ulta lagata hai, ₹6,50,000 inventory ki badhat ko jodta hai, aur ₹8,50,000 finance costs aur interest income ke sign ulte karta hai.

questions.question: Ek fast-growing firm (tax ignore karo) ka net profit ₹6,00,000 hai. Depreciation ₹1,00,000; trade receivables ₹5,50,000 badhe; inventory ₹3,00,000 badhi; trade payables ₹1,00,000 badhe. CFO kitna hai?
questions.explanation: 6,00,000 + 1,00,000 − 5,50,000 − 3,00,000 + 1,00,000 = −₹50,000. Profit hone ke bawajood cash bahar gaya, kyunki paisa receivables aur inventory me phans gaya — profit ≠ cash. −₹1,50,000 depreciation wapas nahi jodta, −₹2,50,000 payables ki badhat ko ghata deta hai, aur ₹14,50,000 working capital ke saare sign ulte kar deta hai.

weeks.title: Cash flow statement: investing, financing and free cash flow
weeks.summary: Is week aap investing aur financing activities classify karna, PPE movement se capital expenditure nikalna, opening se closing cash tak reconcile karna, aur free cash flow ka matlab samajhna seekhoge.
concepts: **Investing activities**: long-term assets aur investments ke cash flows — PPE ya intangible assets khareedna (outflow), purane assets bechna (inflow), doosri companies ke shares/bonds khareedna-bechna, loans dena aur wapas lena. Ind AS 7 ke hisaab se non-financial companies interest aur dividend **received** bhi yahin dikhati hain.

**Financing activities**: owners aur lenders ke saath cash flows — shares issue karna, loans lena (inflow), loans chukana, shares buy back karna, **dividends paid** aur **interest paid** (outflow). Ind AS 7 me non-financial companies ke liye interest paid financing me hi jaata hai. Taxes generally operating me rehte hain.

**Non-cash transactions** cash flow statement me nahi aate: jaise building ke badle shares issue karna, ya loan ko equity me convert karna. Inhe notes me disclose karte hain. Isi tarah depreciation bhi kisi activity me cash flow nahi hai.

**Capex nikalna (PPE movement)**: closing net PPE = opening net PPE + purchases − depreciation − bechi gayi assets ka carrying amount. Isse purchases (capital expenditure) nikalta hai. Bechne par jo cash mila (carrying amount nahi) wo investing inflow hai; gain/loss CFO me adjust ho chuka hai.

**Reconciliation**: net change in cash = CFO + CFI + CFF. Opening cash and cash equivalents + net change = closing cash and cash equivalents, jo balance sheet ke cash figure se match hona chahiye. Ye cash flow statement ka final check hai.

**Free cash flow (FCF)**: is course ki definition — FCF = CFO − capital expenditure (PPE aur intangibles ki purchases). Ye wo cash hai jo business chalane aur assets maintain karne ke baad lenders aur shareholders ke liye bachta hai. Alag-alag analysts alag definitions use karte hain (kuch asset sale proceeds bhi jodte hain), isliye definition hamesha bataani chahiye.

**Pattern padhna**: healthy company me aksar CFO positive, CFI negative (growth ke liye investment), aur CFF positive ya negative (loan lena ya chukana/dividend). Lagataar negative CFO aur positive CFF ka matlab ho sakta hai ki business udhaar par chal raha hai.

example.problem: Fictional company 'Vayu Fans Ltd': opening net PPE ₹10,00,000, closing ₹12,50,000; saal ka depreciation ₹1,50,000; ek machine jiska carrying amount ₹80,000 tha, ₹95,000 cash me bechi. CFO ₹6,00,000. Financing me loan repayment ₹1,00,000 aur dividend paid ₹50,000. Opening cash ₹40,000. Capex, CFI, FCF aur closing cash nikalo.

mistakes: PPE ka sirf net change (closing − opening) ko capex maan lena. Depreciation aur bechi gayi assets ka carrying amount wapas jodo, tabhi asli purchases niklegi.
Asset sale me carrying amount ko investing inflow likhna. Inflow wahi hai jo cash mila (sale proceeds).

Interest paid ko ek jagah operating aur doosri jagah financing me daalna. Ek convention chuno (Ind AS 7 non-financial companies: interest paid financing, interest received investing) aur saare sawalon me wahi lagao.
revision: Investing: PPE, investments, loans given; interest/dividend received.
Financing: shares, borrowings, repayments, dividends paid, interest paid.
Capex = closing PPE − opening PPE + depreciation + carrying amount of disposals.
Opening cash + CFO + CFI + CFF = closing cash.
FCF (is course me) = CFO − capital expenditure.

questions.question: Ek manufacturing company ne apne shareholders ko ₹5,00,000 dividend cash me diya. Cash flow statement me ye kahan aayega?
options: Kahin nahi, kyunki ye P&L item nahi hai
questions.explanation: Dividend owners ko return hai, isliye financing outflow. Ye P&L me nahi hota, par cash to bahar gaya — isliye cash flow statement me zaroor aata hai. Operating ka trap isliye lagta hai kyunki dividend profit se juda hai.

questions.question: Ek company ne doosri company ke shares long-term investment ke liye ₹8,00,000 me khareede. Ye kis activity ka cash flow hai?
options: Cash flow statement me nahi aata
questions.explanation: Doosri company ke shares khareedna ek investment hai ⇒ investing outflow. Financing tab hota jab company **apne** shares issue karti ya buy back karti — yahi sabse common confusion hai.

questions.question: Ek company ke saal me: naye shares issue karke ₹5,00,000 mile; naya loan ₹2,00,000 liya; purana loan ₹3,00,000 chukaya; dividend ₹1,20,000 diya; interest ₹60,000 diya. Interest paid ko financing me rakhte hue, net cash from financing activities kitna hai?
questions.explanation: 5,00,000 + 2,00,000 − 3,00,000 − 1,20,000 − 60,000 = ₹2,20,000. ₹2,80,000 interest ko operating me daalne se aata hai, ₹3,40,000 dividend chhodne se, aur ₹11,80,000 sab amounts ko jodne se (outflows ko bhi plus maan liya).

questions.question: Ek company ka CFO ₹4,20,000, CFI −₹6,50,000 aur CFF ₹1,80,000 hai. Opening cash and cash equivalents ₹1,10,000 the. Closing cash and cash equivalents kitne honge?
questions.explanation: Net change = 4,20,000 − 6,50,000 + 1,80,000 = −50,000. Closing = 1,10,000 − 50,000 = ₹60,000. −₹50,000 sirf net change hai (opening jodna bhool gaye), ₹1,60,000 net change ka sign ulta lene se, aur ₹13,60,000 CFI ko positive maanne se aata hai.

questions.question: Ek company ka CFO ₹9,00,000 hai. Saal me PPE par ₹5,50,000 kharch hue, purane assets bech kar ₹50,000 mile, aur ₹1,00,000 dividend diya. FCF = CFO − capital expenditure definition se free cash flow kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Definition ke hisaab se sirf capex ghatao: 9,00,000 − 5,50,000 = ₹3,50,000. ₹4,00,000 asset sale proceeds ko capex se net karne se aata hai (wo alag definition hai), aur ₹2,50,000 dividend bhi ghatane se — dividend FCF ka use hai, FCF ko kam nahi karta.

questions.question: Ek company ka opening net PPE ₹20,00,000 aur closing net PPE ₹23,00,000 hai. Saal ka depreciation ₹2,50,000 tha. Ek asset jiska carrying amount ₹1,00,000 tha, ₹70,000 cash me becha gaya. Agar koi aur investing item nahi hai, to net cash from investing activities kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Purchases = 23,00,000 − 20,00,000 + 2,50,000 + 1,00,000 = 6,50,000. CFI = −6,50,000 + 70,000 = −₹5,80,000. −₹6,50,000 sale proceeds bhoolne se, −₹3,00,000 sirf PPE ka net change lene se, aur −₹5,50,000 carrying amount (1,00,000) ko cash inflow maanne se aata hai.

questions.question: Ek company ne bank se 5 saal ka ₹10,00,000 ka term loan liya. Cash flow statement me ye kahan aayega?
options: Kahin nahi, kyunki ye liability hai
questions.explanation: Loan lena lenders ke saath cash flow hai, isliye financing inflow. Investing long-term assets ke liye hai — loan se asset khareedoge to wo alag investing outflow hoga. 'Liability hai to kahin nahi' galat hai: cash asal me aaya hai.

questions.question: Ek company ne ₹50,00,000 ki building ke badle seller ko apne shares issue kiye; koi cash nahi diya gaya. Cash flow statement me iska treatment kya hai?
options: Kisi activity me nahi; notes me non-cash transaction ke roop me disclose
questions.explanation: Cash hila hi nahi, isliye ye cash flow statement me kisi activity me nahi aata; non-cash transaction ke roop me notes me disclose hota hai. Investing aur financing dono me dikhana ek aisa cash flow bana deta hai jo hua hi nahi.

questions.question: Ek manufacturing company ko fixed deposit par ₹40,000 interest mila. Course ke convention (Ind AS 7, non-financial company) ke hisaab se ye kis activity me aayega?
options: Cash flow statement me nahi aata
questions.explanation: Non-financial companies interest aur dividend received ko investing me dikhati hain — ye investments se aaya return hai. Interest paid financing me jaata hai, isliye 'financing' wala option paid aur received ko mix kar deta hai. Indirect method me interest income CFO se isi wajah se ghatayi jaati hai.

questions.question: Ek company ke saal ke items: machinery khareedi ₹7,00,000; purani vehicle ₹1,20,000 cash me bechi (carrying amount ₹90,000); doosri company ke shares ₹2,00,000 me khareede; dividend received ₹30,000; FD interest received ₹20,000. Net cash from investing activities kitna hai?
questions.explanation: CFI = −7,00,000 + 1,20,000 − 2,00,000 + 30,000 + 20,000 = −₹7,30,000. Inflow wahi jo cash mila (1,20,000), carrying amount nahi — ₹90,000 lene se −₹7,60,000 aata hai. −₹7,80,000 dividend aur interest received ko chhod deta hai, aur −₹8,20,000 sirf gain (30,000) ko inflow maan leta hai.

questions.question: Ek company: CFO ₹12,00,000; PPE ki purchases ₹6,50,000; software (intangible) ki purchase ₹1,00,000; purane asset ki sale se ₹80,000 mile; naya loan ₹3,00,000 liya. FCF = CFO − capital expenditure definition se free cash flow kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Capex = PPE + intangibles = 6,50,000 + 1,00,000 = 7,50,000. FCF = 12,00,000 − 7,50,000 = ₹4,50,000. ₹5,30,000 sale proceeds bhi jod deta hai (course definition me nahi), ₹5,50,000 intangibles ko capex nahi maanta, aur ₹7,50,000 loan ko bhi jod deta hai — loan financing hai, free cash nahi.

questions.question: Ek company ka opening net PPE ₹40,00,000 aur closing net PPE ₹46,00,000 hai. Saal ka depreciation ₹5,00,000 tha. Ek asset jiska carrying amount ₹3,00,000 tha, ₹3,60,000 cash me becha gaya. Koi aur investing item nahi. Capex aur net cash from investing activities kitne hain?
questions.explanation: 46,00,000 = 40,00,000 + purchases − 5,00,000 − 3,00,000 ⇒ purchases = ₹14,00,000. CFI = −14,00,000 + 3,60,000 (sale proceeds) = −₹10,40,000. ₹6,00,000 sirf PPE ka net change hai, −₹11,00,000 carrying amount ko inflow maanta hai, aur ₹11,00,000 bechi gayi asset ka carrying amount wapas jodna bhool jaata hai.

questions.question: Ek company ke saal ke cash flows: CFO ₹8,00,000; capex ₹9,50,000; asset sale se ₹1,50,000; interest received ₹50,000; naye shares se ₹4,00,000; loan repayment ₹2,50,000; interest paid ₹1,00,000; dividend paid ₹1,50,000. Closing cash and cash equivalents ₹3,20,000 hain. Opening cash and cash equivalents kitne the?

Ek company ki total borrowings opening ₹25,00,000 aur closing ₹30,00,000 hain. Saal me ₹8,00,000 ke loans chukaye gaye; baaki badlav naye loans se aaya. Interest paid ₹2,40,000 aur dividend paid ₹1,60,000; koi share issue nahi hua. Interest paid financing me rakhte hue, naye loans kitne liye gaye aur CFF kitna hai?
questions.explanation: 30,00,000 = 25,00,000 + naye loans − 8,00,000 ⇒ naye loans = ₹13,00,000. CFF = 13,00,000 − 8,00,000 − 2,40,000 − 1,60,000 = ₹1,00,000. Naya loan ₹5,00,000 net change ko hi naya loan maanta hai aur phir repayment dobara ghatata hai (CFF −₹7,00,000); CFF ₹3,40,000 interest paid ko financing se bahar kar deta hai; CFF ₹5,00,000 sirf loans ka net hai, interest aur dividend bhool jaata hai.

questions.question: Ek company (indirect method): PBT ₹10,00,000; depreciation ₹3,00,000; trade receivables ₹2,00,000 badhe; trade payables ₹50,000 badhe; income tax paid ₹2,50,000. Opening net PPE ₹30,00,000, closing ₹34,00,000; saal me koi asset nahi becha. FCF = CFO − capex se free cash flow kitna hai?

weeks.title: Ratio analysis: liquidity and solvency
weeks.summary: Is week aap ratios se company ki short-term paying capacity (current, quick, cash ratio) aur long-term strength (debt-equity, interest coverage) naapna seekhoge, aur samjhoge ki transactions in ratios ko kaise badalte hain.
concepts: **Ratio analysis kyun**: absolute numbers (₹50 lakh profit) akele kuch nahi batate — ek chhoti aur ek badi company ko compare karne ke liye ratios chahiye. Ratios ko teen tarah padho: company ke pichhle saalon se (trend), same industry ki companies se, aur business ki nature ke saath. Ek ratio kabhi akele final verdict nahi deta.

**Liquidity** = kya company agle 12 mahine ki obligations time par chuka paayegi? **Solvency** = kya company lambe samay tak apna debt aur interest sambhal paayegi? Liquidity ke liye current items, solvency ke liye capital structure aur earnings dekhte hain.

**Current ratio** = current assets ÷ current liabilities. Traditional rule of thumb 2 : 1 hai, par ye industry par depend karta hai — jaldi bikne wale maal wale retailers kam ratio par bhi aaram se chalte hain. Bahut zyada ratio ka matlab idle cash ya phansi inventory bhi ho sakta hai.

**Quick (acid-test) ratio** = (current assets − inventories − prepaid expenses) ÷ current liabilities. Inventory bechne me time lagta hai aur prepaid se cash wapas nahi aata, isliye inhe hatate hain. **Cash ratio** = (cash + marketable securities) ÷ current liabilities — sabse strict test.

**Debt-equity ratio** = total borrowings ÷ total equity. Is course ka convention: borrowings me long-term, short-term aur current maturities — saare interest-bearing loans; equity = share capital + other equity. Zyada D/E matlab zyada financial risk, par sahi level industry par depend karta hai (infrastructure me zyada, software me kam).

**Interest coverage ratio** = EBIT ÷ finance costs (interest). Batata hai ki operating profit interest ko kitni baar cover karta hai. 1 se kam matlab operating profit se interest bhi nahi nikal raha. Lenders iske saath debt service coverage (interest + principal repayment ko cover karna) bhi dekhte hain.

**Transactions ka asar aur limits**: agar current ratio 1 se zyada hai, to current asset se current liability chukane par (jaise cash se creditors) ratio **badh** jaata hai; 1 se kam ho to ghatta hai. Companies year-end se pehle aise moves karke ratios sundar dikha sakti hain (**window dressing**). Balance sheet ek din ki photo hai, isliye average aur trend dekhna behtar hai.

example.problem: Fictional company 'Meru Foods Ltd': inventories ₹4,00,000; prepaid expenses ₹50,000; trade receivables ₹5,00,000; cash ₹2,50,000; trade payables ₹4,00,000; short-term borrowings ₹2,00,000; long-term borrowings ₹10,00,000; total equity ₹15,00,000; EBIT ₹4,80,000; finance costs ₹1,20,000. Current, quick, cash, debt-equity aur interest coverage ratio nikalo.
steps: Answer: **current 2.00, quick 1.25, cash 0.42, D/E 0.80, interest coverage 4 times** — liquidity theek, debt moderate.

mistakes: Quick ratio me sirf inventory hatana aur prepaid expenses bhool jaana. Prepaid se cash wapas nahi aata, use bhi hatao.
Debt-equity me equity ki jagah sirf share capital lena. Equity = share capital + other equity (reserves), warna ratio bahut zyada dikhega.
Interest coverage me PBT use karna. PBT me interest pehle hi ghat chuka hai; EBIT (interest se pehle) lo.
revision: Current ratio = CA ÷ CL.
Quick ratio = (CA − inventories − prepaid) ÷ CL.
D/E = total borrowings ÷ total equity.
Interest coverage = EBIT ÷ finance costs.
CR > 1 ho to CA se CL chukane par CR badhta hai.

questions.question: Ek company ke current assets ₹6,00,000 aur current liabilities ₹4,00,000 hain. Current ratio kya hai?
questions.explanation: Current ratio = 6,00,000 ÷ 4,00,000 = 1.50. 0.67 ratio ko ulta (CL ÷ CA) lene se aata hai, aur 0.50 working capital (2,00,000) ko CL se divide karne se.

questions.question: Ek company ke current assets ₹6,00,000 hain, jinme inventories ₹2,00,000 aur prepaid expenses ₹20,000 shaamil hain. Current liabilities ₹4,00,000. Quick ratio kya hai?
questions.explanation: Quick assets = 6,00,000 − 2,00,000 − 20,000 = 3,80,000. Quick ratio = 3,80,000 ÷ 4,00,000 = 0.95. 1.00 tab aata hai jab sirf inventory hatate ho aur prepaid bhool jaate ho; 1.50 current ratio hai.

questions.question: Ek company: long-term borrowings ₹12,00,000; short-term borrowings ₹3,00,000; equity share capital ₹10,00,000; other equity ₹15,00,000. Debt = saari borrowings maan kar debt-equity ratio kya hai?
questions.explanation: Debt = 12,00,000 + 3,00,000 = 15,00,000; equity = 10,00,000 + 15,00,000 = 25,00,000. D/E = 0.60. 0.48 short-term borrowings chhodne se aata hai, aur 1.50 equity me sirf share capital lene se.

questions.question: Ek company ka EBIT ₹9,00,000 aur finance costs ₹1,50,000 hain. Interest coverage ratio kya hai?
questions.explanation: Interest coverage = EBIT ÷ interest = 9,00,000 ÷ 1,50,000 = 6 times. 5 times PBT (7,50,000) use karne se aata hai — PBT me interest pehle hi ghat chuka hai. 0.17 ratio ulta lene se.

questions.question: Ek company ke current assets ₹4,00,000 aur current liabilities ₹2,00,000 hain (current ratio 2.00). Wo ₹50,000 cash dekar trade payables chukati hai. Ab current ratio ka kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Dono side 50,000 ghatte hain: 3,50,000 ÷ 1,50,000 = 2.33. Ratio 1 se zyada ho to numerator aur denominator se same amount ghatane par ratio badhta hai. 1.75 sirf cash ghatane se, aur 2.67 sirf payables ghatane se aata hai — ek hi side badalna galat hai.

questions.question: Ek company ka current ratio 2.5 hai aur working capital ₹6,00,000 hai. Inventories ₹3,00,000 hain aur koi prepaid expense nahi hai. Quick ratio kya hai?
questions.explanation: CA = 2.5 × CL aur CA − CL = 6,00,000 ⇒ 1.5 × CL = 6,00,000 ⇒ CL = 4,00,000, CA = 10,00,000. Quick = (10,00,000 − 3,00,000) ÷ 4,00,000 = 1.75. 2.50 current ratio hi hai, 0.75 inventory ÷ CL hai, aur 1.17 quick assets ko working capital se divide karne ka trap hai.

questions.question: Ek company ke paas cash ₹1,20,000 aur marketable securities ₹30,000 hain. Current liabilities ₹3,00,000 hain. Cash ratio kya hai?
questions.explanation: Cash ratio = (cash + marketable securities) ÷ current liabilities = 1,50,000 ÷ 3,00,000 = 0.50. 0.40 marketable securities bhool jaata hai, 2.00 ulta divide karta hai, aur 0.10 sirf securities leta hai.

questions.question: Ek company ka interest coverage ratio 0.8 times hai. Iska kya matlab hai?
options: Current assets current liabilities ke 0.8 guna hain
Company ka debt uski equity ka 80% hai
Operating profit (EBIT) se interest bhi poora nahi nikal raha
questions.explanation: Interest coverage = EBIT ÷ interest. 0.8 ka matlab EBIT interest se bhi kam hai — 1 se kam hona solvency ka red flag hai. Doosra option current ratio ki baat hai, teesra debt-equity ki, aur chautha decimal galat padhta hai.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa ratio company ki **solvency** (lambe samay tak debt sambhalne ki capacity) measure karta hai?
questions.explanation: Solvency capital structure dekhti hai — kitna debt hai equity ke muqable — isliye debt-equity ratio. Current, quick aur cash ratio teeno liquidity ratios hain, jo agle 12 mahine ki obligations ke liye current items dekhte hain.

questions.question: Ek company: long-term borrowings ₹18,00,000; current maturities of long-term debt ₹2,00,000; short-term borrowings ₹5,00,000; trade payables ₹6,00,000; equity share capital ₹8,00,000; other equity ₹12,00,000. Course convention se debt-equity ratio kya hai?
questions.explanation: Debt = saare interest-bearing loans = 18,00,000 + 2,00,000 + 5,00,000 = 25,00,000. Equity = 8,00,000 + 12,00,000 = 20,00,000. D/E = 1.25. 1.55 trade payables ko bhi debt maanta hai (wo interest-bearing nahi), 3.13 sirf share capital ko equity leta hai, aur 0.90 sirf long-term borrowings leta hai.

questions.question: Ek company ke current assets ₹4,00,000 aur current liabilities ₹5,00,000 hain (current ratio 0.80). Wo ₹1,00,000 cash dekar trade payables chukati hai. Ab current ratio ka kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Naya ratio = (4,00,000 − 1,00,000) ÷ (5,00,000 − 1,00,000) = 3,00,000 ÷ 4,00,000 = 0.75. Ratio 1 se kam ho to barabar amount dono se ghatane par ratio aur girta hai. 'Payment se ratio hamesha sudharta hai' wala trap sirf tab sahi hai jab ratio 1 se zyada ho.

questions.question: Ek company ke items: inventories ₹6,00,000; prepaid expenses ₹40,000; trade receivables ₹4,60,000; cash ₹1,00,000; trade payables ₹3,50,000; short-term borrowings ₹3,50,000; long-term borrowings ₹9,00,000; total equity ₹15,00,000. Quick ratio aur debt-equity ratio kya hain?
questions.explanation: Current assets = 6,00,000 + 40,000 + 4,60,000 + 1,00,000 = 12,00,000; current liabilities = 7,00,000. Quick = (12,00,000 − 6,00,000 − 40,000) ÷ 7,00,000 = 0.80. D/E = (9,00,000 + 3,50,000) ÷ 15,00,000 = 0.83. 0.86 prepaid hatana bhool jaata hai, 0.60 sirf long-term borrowings leta hai, aur 1.71 current ratio hai.

questions.question: Ek company ka PAT ₹9,00,000 hai, tax rate PBT ka 25% hai, aur finance costs ₹2,00,000 hain. Koi other income ya exceptional item nahi. Interest coverage ratio kya hai?
questions.explanation: PBT = 9,00,000 ÷ 75% = 12,00,000. EBIT = PBT + interest = 14,00,000. Coverage = 14,00,000 ÷ 2,00,000 = 7 times. 6 times PBT use karta hai (interest pehle hi ghat chuka), 4.5 times PAT use karta hai, aur 5.5 times PAT me interest jodta hai par tax wapas nahi jodta.

questions.question: Ek company ka current ratio 2.4 aur quick ratio 1.5 hai. Current liabilities ₹5,00,000 hain aur koi prepaid expense nahi hai. Inventories kitni hain?
questions.explanation: Current assets = 2.4 × 5,00,000 = 12,00,000. Quick assets = 1.5 × 5,00,000 = 7,50,000. Prepaid nahi hai, to inventory = 12,00,000 − 7,50,000 = ₹4,50,000 (ya seedha (2.4 − 1.5) × 5,00,000). ₹7,50,000 quick assets hain, ₹7,00,000 working capital hai (12,00,000 − 5,00,000), aur ₹12,00,000 poore current assets.

questions.question: Ek company ke current assets ₹12,00,000 aur current liabilities ₹8,00,000 hain (current ratio 1.5). Year-end se pehle wo ₹2,00,000 ka sirf ek transaction karegi. Kis transaction ke baad current ratio sabse zyada hoga?
options: ₹2,00,000 ka short-term loan lekar cash bank me rakhna
questions.explanation: Payables chukana: 10,00,000 ÷ 6,00,000 = 1.67 (ratio 1 se upar hai, isliye badhta hai — window dressing). Machinery: 10,00,000 ÷ 8,00,000 = 1.25. Short-term loan ya credit inventory: 14,00,000 ÷ 10,00,000 = 1.40 — dono taraf barabar badhne se ratio 1 ki taraf girta hai. Isliye year-end ki ek photo par bharosa na karke trend dekho.

weeks.title: Ratio analysis: profitability, efficiency and DuPont
weeks.summary: Is week aap margins aur return ratios (ROA, ROE, ROCE), turnover aur days ratios, cash conversion cycle, aur DuPont analysis se ROE ko margin, efficiency aur leverage me todna seekhoge — aur teeno statements ko saath padhna.
concepts: **Margins**: gross margin = GP ÷ revenue; operating (EBIT) margin = EBIT ÷ revenue; **net profit margin** = PAT ÷ revenue. Har ₹100 ki sale me se kitna bacha — ye batate hain. Margin girna pricing pressure ya badhte costs ka signal ho sakta hai.

**Return ratios**: **ROA** = PAT ÷ average total assets (assets kitna kama rahe hain). **ROE** = PAT ÷ average equity (shareholders ke paise par return). **ROCE** = EBIT ÷ capital employed; is course me capital employed = equity + non-current borrowings. Balance sheet items ke liye opening aur closing ka average lena behtar hai, kyunki profit poore saal me bana.

**Turnover aur days**: asset turnover = revenue ÷ average total assets. Inventory turnover = COGS ÷ average inventory; **days inventory outstanding (DIO)** = 365 ÷ inventory turnover. Receivables turnover = credit revenue ÷ average receivables; **DSO** = average receivables ÷ credit revenue × 365. Payables days (DPO) = average payables ÷ COGS (ya purchases) × 365. Is course me saal = 365 din.

**Cash conversion cycle (CCC)** = DIO + DSO − DPO. Matlab: supplier ko paisa dene se customer se paisa aane tak cash kitne din phansa rehta hai. CCC chhota ⇒ kam working capital chahiye. Kuch businesses (jo customers se pehle paisa le lete hain) ka CCC negative bhi ho sakta hai.

**DuPont analysis**: ROE = net profit margin × asset turnover × equity multiplier = (PAT ÷ revenue) × (revenue ÷ assets) × (assets ÷ equity). Isse pata chalta hai ki ROE kahan se aa raha hai — achhe margin se, assets ke efficient use se, ya zyada debt (leverage) se. Leverage se aaya ROE zyada risky hai.

**Statements ko saath padhna**: profit badh raha hai par CFO gir raha hai aur receivables tezi se badh rahe hain — to earnings ki quality par sawaal hai. Accha practice: PAT ko CFO se compare karo, margins aur days ratios ka trend dekho, aur hamesha same industry se compare karo. Ratios sawaal poochhne ka tool hain, jawab notes aur MD&A me milta hai.

example.problem: Fictional company 'Nila Furnishings Ltd': revenue ₹60,00,000; PAT ₹6,00,000; average total assets ₹40,00,000; average equity ₹25,00,000. DuPont se ROE nikalo aur direct ROE se check karo.
steps: Direct check: 6,00,000 ÷ 25,00,000 = 24% ✓. ROA = 10% × 1.5 = 15%, aur leverage (1.6) use 24% tak le jaata hai.

mistakes: Ratio me sirf closing balance lena jabki opening aur closing dono diye hain. Profit poore saal ka hai, isliye denominator me average lo.
DSO aur turnover ko mix karna: turnover 'kitni baar' hai, days 'kitne din'. 365 ÷ turnover = days.
Zyada ROE ko hamesha achha samajhna. DuPont se dekho — agar ROE sirf equity multiplier (debt) se badha hai to risk bhi badha hai.
revision: NPM = PAT ÷ revenue; ROE = PAT ÷ average equity; ROA = PAT ÷ average assets.
ROCE = EBIT ÷ (equity + non-current borrowings).
DIO = 365 ÷ (COGS ÷ average inventory); DSO = average receivables ÷ credit revenue × 365.
CCC = DIO + DSO − DPO.
DuPont: ROE = NPM × asset turnover × equity multiplier.

questions.question: Ek company ka revenue ₹30,00,000 aur PAT ₹4,50,000 hai. Net profit margin kya hai?
questions.explanation: NPM = 4,50,000 ÷ 30,00,000 = 15%. 6.67 ratio ulta (revenue ÷ PAT) lene se aata hai, aur 85% wo hissa hai jo profit nahi bana.

questions.question: Ek company ka COGS ₹36,00,000 hai. Opening inventory ₹5,00,000 aur closing inventory ₹7,00,000. Saal = 365 din. Days inventory outstanding (DIO) lagbhag kitne hain?
questions.explanation: Average inventory = (5,00,000 + 7,00,000) ÷ 2 = 6,00,000. Turnover = 36,00,000 ÷ 6,00,000 = 6 times. DIO = 365 ÷ 6 ≈ 60.8 ≈ 61 din. 6 turnover hai, din nahi; 71 din sirf closing inventory lene se aur 51 din sirf opening lene se aata hai.

questions.question: Ek company ka PAT ₹5,00,000 hai. Equity saal ki shuruaat me ₹18,00,000 aur end me ₹22,00,000 thi. Average equity par ROE kya hai?
questions.explanation: Average equity = (18,00,000 + 22,00,000) ÷ 2 = 20,00,000. ROE = 5,00,000 ÷ 20,00,000 = 25%. 22.7% sirf closing equity se, 27.8% sirf opening se, aur 12.5% dono ko jod kar 2 se divide na karne se aata hai.

questions.question: Ek company ki saari sales credit par hain: revenue ₹73,00,000. Trade receivables saal ki shuruaat me ₹10,00,000 aur end me ₹14,00,000 the. Saal = 365 din. Average receivables par DSO kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Average receivables = (10,00,000 + 14,00,000) ÷ 2 = 12,00,000. DSO = 12,00,000 ÷ 73,00,000 × 365 = 60 din. 70 din closing aur 50 din opening receivables lene se aata hai; 6.08 receivables turnover hai (kitni baar), din nahi.

questions.question: Ek retailer ke DIO 45 din, DSO 30 din aur DPO 40 din hain. Cash conversion cycle kitne din ka hai?
questions.explanation: CCC = DIO + DSO − DPO = 45 + 30 − 40 = 35 din. 115 din teeno ko jodne se aata hai — supplier ka credit (DPO) cash ko der se bahar bhejta hai, isliye ghatta hai. 55 aur 25 galat terms ghatane se aate hain.

questions.question: Ek company ka net profit margin 8%, asset turnover 2 aur equity multiplier 1.5 hai. Wo zyada debt leti hai: equity multiplier 2.5 ho jaata hai, extra interest se net profit margin 6% reh jaata hai, asset turnover 2 hi rehta hai. Naya ROE kya hai?
questions.explanation: DuPont: naya ROE = 6% × 2 × 2.5 = 30% (pehle 8% × 2 × 1.5 = 24% tha). 40% tab aata hai jab margin ka girna (8% → 6%) bhool jaate ho; 12% sirf ROA (NPM × asset turnover) hai. Dhyaan do: ROE badha, par sirf leverage se — risk bhi badha.

questions.question: Ek company ka revenue ₹90,00,000 aur average total assets ₹60,00,000 hain. Asset turnover kya hai?
questions.explanation: Asset turnover = revenue ÷ average total assets = 90,00,000 ÷ 60,00,000 = 1.5 times — har ₹1 ke asset se ₹1.5 ki sale. 0.67 ulta divide karta hai, aur 15 / 0.15 decimal ki galtiyan hain.

questions.question: DuPont analysis me ROE ko kin teen hisson me toda jaata hai?
options: Gross margin × inventory turnover × equity multiplier
Net profit margin + asset turnover + equity multiplier
Net profit margin × asset turnover × equity multiplier
questions.explanation: ROE = (PAT ÷ revenue) × (revenue ÷ assets) × (assets ÷ equity). Sirf pehle do ka product ROA hai, ROE nahi — leverage wala hissa chhoot jaata hai. Gross margin aur inventory turnover DuPont ke hisse nahi, aur teeno ko jodna (multiply ki jagah) koi meaningful number nahi deta.

questions.question: Ek company ka receivables turnover 8 times hai. Saal = 365 din. DSO lagbhag kitne din hai?
questions.explanation: DSO = 365 ÷ receivables turnover = 365 ÷ 8 ≈ 45.6, yaani lagbhag 46 din. 8 turnover ko hi days maan leta hai ('kitni baar' vs 'kitne din' ka mix), 2,920 divide ki jagah multiply karta hai, aur 4.6 decimal ki galti hai.

questions.question: Ek company ka EBIT ₹18,00,000 hai. Equity ₹70,00,000, non-current borrowings ₹50,00,000 aur current liabilities ₹20,00,000 hain. Course ki definition (capital employed = equity + non-current borrowings) se ROCE kya hai?
questions.explanation: Capital employed = 70,00,000 + 50,00,000 = 1,20,00,000. ROCE = 18,00,000 ÷ 1,20,00,000 = 15%. 25.71% sirf equity leta hai (wo ROE jaisa ho jaata hai), 12.86% current liabilities bhi jod deta hai, aur 36% sirf borrowings leta hai.

questions.question: Ek company ke DIO 50 din aur DSO 35 din hain. Average trade payables ₹6,00,000 aur COGS ₹73,00,000 hai. Saal = 365 din. Cash conversion cycle kitne din ka hai?
questions.explanation: DPO = 6,00,000 ÷ 73,00,000 × 365 = 30 din. CCC = DIO + DSO − DPO = 50 + 35 − 30 = 55 din. 115 DPO ko jod deta hai, 85 DPO ko bhool jaata hai, aur 20 DSO ko chhod deta hai.

questions.question: Ek company: revenue ₹1,20,00,000; PAT ₹9,00,000; total assets opening ₹70,00,000, closing ₹90,00,000; equity opening ₹28,00,000, closing ₹32,00,000. Averages use karke DuPont se ROE aur equity multiplier kya hain?
questions.explanation: Average assets = 80,00,000; average equity = 30,00,000. Margin = 9,00,000 ÷ 1,20,00,000 = 7.5%; asset turnover = 1.5; equity multiplier = 80 ÷ 30 = 2.67. ROE = 7.5% × 1.5 × 2.67 = 30% (check: 9 ÷ 30). 28.13% / 2.81 sirf closing balances leta hai, 32.14% / 2.50 sirf opening, aur 11.25% ROA hai jisme leverage chhoot gaya.

questions.question: Ek company ki saari sales credit par hain: revenue ₹1,46,00,000; COGS ₹1,09,50,000; average inventory ₹18,00,000; average receivables ₹20,00,000; average trade payables ₹15,00,000. Saal = 365 din, aur DPO COGS par nikalo. Cash conversion cycle kitne din ka hai?
questions.explanation: DIO = 18,00,000 ÷ 1,09,50,000 × 365 = 60. DSO = 20,00,000 ÷ 1,46,00,000 × 365 = 50. DPO = 15,00,000 ÷ 1,09,50,000 × 365 = 50. CCC = 60 + 50 − 50 = 60 din. 160 DPO ko jod deta hai, 45 DIO ko revenue par nikalta hai (COGS par nikalna chahiye), aur 72.5 DPO ko revenue par.

questions.question: Do companies X aur Y dono ka ROE 20% hai. X: net profit margin 10%, asset turnover 1.25, equity multiplier 1.6. Y: net profit margin 5%, asset turnover 1.0. Y ka equity multiplier kitna hai, aur DuPont ke hisaab se kiska ROE zyada risky hai?
options: Y ka multiplier 4.0; Y ka ROE zyada risky
Y ka multiplier 1.6; dono barabar risky
Y ka multiplier 4.0; X ka ROE zyada risky
Y ka multiplier 0.25; X ka ROE zyada risky
questions.explanation: X check: 10% × 1.25 × 1.6 = 20%. Y: 20% = 5% × 1.0 × EM ⇒ EM = 4.0. Y ka ROE kam margin aur kam turnover ke bawajood bahut zyada leverage (debt) se aa raha hai, isliye zyada risky. 'Dono barabar' maan leta hai ki same ROE matlab same quality; 0.25 ulta divide karne se aata hai.

questions.question: Ek company ka revenue ₹80,00,000 aur gross margin 25% hai. Opening inventory ₹9,00,000 aur closing inventory ₹11,00,000. Saal = 365 din. Average inventory par inventory turnover aur DIO kitne hain?
questions.explanation: COGS = 80,00,000 × (1 − 25%) = 60,00,000. Average inventory = 10,00,000. Turnover = 6 times; DIO = 365 ÷ 6 ≈ 61 din. 8 times revenue se divide karta hai (COGS lena chahiye), 5.45 sirf closing inventory leta hai, aur 2 times gross profit (20,00,000) ko COGS maan leta hai.
